Wider Sports News.title: ‘Sham’ contracts and inflated sponsorship revenue: What next for Man City after landmark Premier League verdict?
Wider Sports News.summary: As the club maintain their innocence, the sporting, commercial and financial effects have only begun to reverberate. The post ‘Sham’ contracts and inflated sponsorship revenue: What next for Man City after landmark Premier League verdict? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The story of the biggest financial scandal in English soccer history is by now a familiar saga, but it has not lost its capacity to shock. Last week, reports started to emerge that Manchester City had been found guilty by an independent commission of 114 of the 115 charges levelled against the club in 2023 for extensive breaches of its cost-control rules. Those leaks meant that when the Premier League’s official confirmation eventually arrived on 29th September, it came as no surprise.

But the scale of City’s deception and the severity of the language in both the league’s statement was unprecedented. The investigation determined City worked to ‘artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than UK£900 million’ between 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, a period in which they won three of their eight Premier League titles.

Wider Sports News.summary: HSBC Goes Big-Wave Surfing to Make a Splash with ‘The Right Wave’ — LBB LBB - Little Black Book
Wider Sports News.body:
HSBC has launched a hero brand film ‘The Right Wave’ to bring to life its role as a trusted banking partner for its customers. The cinematic hero film explores the extreme, high-pressure dynamics between a big-wave surfer, Matahi Drollet and a jet ski driver, Tahurai Henry, as they conquer overwhelming 25ft swells. Drawing on the relationship between Matahi and Tahurai, the film symbolises HSBC’s role in bringing expertise, and deep understanding of the world’s changing currents to build the right conditions for customer success.

The film was shot on Tahiti’s renowned surf break Teahupoʻo during several high-risk wave breaks. Produced by Superprime Films, the team collaborated with local Polynesian production company, We Are Ora to draw on Teahupo’o’s local and specialist knowledge to capture the best possible wave conditions. It was directed by the celebrated filmmaker Kiku Ohe alongside cinematographers Tim Lorentzen and Morgan Maassen.

Wider Sports News.title: SportAccord’s Kelly Fairweather on rebuilding relevance in sport’s new reality
Wider Sports News.summary: Nearly one year after joining SportAccord as managing director from the ITF, Kelly Fairweather discusses the challenges facing federations today and how the upcoming SportAccord Forum has been designed to help navigate them. The post SportAccord’s Kelly Fairweather on rebuilding relevance in sport’s new reality appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
When Kelly Fairweather took over as managing director of SportAccord last year, he arrived having viewed the international sports ecosystem from several vantage points. The South African spent nearly a decade as sports director of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) before a brief stint at the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), where his remit included overseeing relations with international federations (IFs). Fairweather went on to run two of those IFs, first as chief executive of the International Hockey Federation (IHF), followed by the same role at the International Tennis Federation (ITF).

Having sat both alongside and across the table from IFs, Fairweather has firsthand insight into what those federations need from an event organiser like SportAccord, which has served as a meeting place for the international sports community for more than two decades.

Rugby.title: Swys de Bruin's post-Springbok Women role has been confirmed
Rugby.summary: Swys de Bruin has taken up his first coaching role since leaving his position as Springbok Women head coach last month.
Rugby.body:
Swys de Bruin has taken up his first coaching role since leaving his position as Springbok Women head coach last month. The 66-year-old has joined Paarl Boys’ High School as their head of coaching.

It is a position that his son, Neil, vacated in December 2025 to join the Blue Bulls as their attack coach in the United Rugby Championship. At the start of September, ahead of the Springbok Women’s clash with the Black Ferns in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry, it was confirmed that De Bruin had abruptly vacated his role as head coach.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock addresses LA28 Olympic rumours head on
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock has said that representing Great Britain Sevens at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is “definitely something I’m aspiring to do”.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock has said that representing Great Britain Sevens at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is “definitely something I’m aspiring to do”. The Northampton Saints and England back-row has been linked with a place in a prospective Great Britain squad alongside Marcus Smith, Tommy Freeman, Henry Arundell and Noah Caluori. RugbyPass reported in July that the quintet had been targeted with LA28 in mind.

Pollock’s immediate priority remains next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia, but, speaking during a Q&A on his YouTube channel, the 21-year-old made no secret of the appeal of following the path taken by Antoine Dupont, who switched his focus to sevens before helping France win Olympic gold on home soil in Paris in 2024.

Rugby.title: 'Rugby needs to be demystified to attract new fans and fresh investment'
Rugby.summary: The inaugural Nations Championship represents the first major opportunity to embrace private investment, but only if the game is accessible.
Rugby.body:
Money has always been a slightly dirty word in rugby. It was the original reason union and league went their separate ways back in 1895. It took union another 100 years to finally admit players deserved to be paid for their time. It was 90 years behind football in that respect, as highlighted by an excerpt from the following piece written by ex-Ireland international Andrew Trimble and Dan McKeown.

“Football made its peace with money in 1885, when the FA legalised professionalism in England rather than lose the northern clubs that were already paying players. Football has been learning how to run a professional sport for 140 years, rugby has been learning for 30. The governance philosophy in rugby union was designed for the amateur century, and is now being asked to do a job it was explicitly built to prevent.”

Rugby.title: Scotland name 32-player squad for two-match Australia tour
Rugby.summary: Interim head coach Dave Butcher has named the 32-player Scotland squad that will travel to Australia to play the Wallaroos in two Tests.
Rugby.body:
Interim head coach Dave Butcher has named the 32-player Scotland squad that will travel to Australia to play the Wallaroos in two Tests. In October, Scotland did not win in any of the three Test matches that they played. Heavy losses to Canada and the Black Ferns were followed by a 30-10 loss to Australia in Edinburgh, with Scotland hoping they can turn the tide in their three-match series in the Wallaroos.

The squad does not contain Emma Wassell and Alex Stewart, who sustained campaign ending injuries. There is a place for Rachel Philipps who has returned after going through concussion protocols.

Rugby.title: PWR lock in Final venue through 2029 in bid to ‘build something special’
Rugby.summary: JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby have confirmed that The Stoop will host the competition's showpiece finale in 2027, 2028 and 2029.
Rugby.body:
JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby have confirmed that The Stoop will host the competition’s showpiece final in 2027, 2028 and 2029. The home of Harlequins welcomed more than 8,000 supporters at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season, when Saracens ended their four-year wait for an English league title with a 52-14 victory over Trailfinders Women.

The West London venue, which sits across the road from Allianz Stadium, will now become the long-term host for the PWR Final as the league aims to establish an annual flagship event for supporters.

Rugby.body:
Marlie Packer will not travel with the Red Roses to North America for the latter half of the WXV Global Series ahead of the birth of her first child with Rosie Galligan. The 37-year-old flanker, who has won 119 Test caps, played in all three of England’s home fixtures in September and started in the team’s win against the Black Ferns at Allianz Stadium.

Of the 32 players selected by John Mitchell for the tour, 24 played in fixtures against Australia, Canada and New Zealand. The squad does not include Delaney Burns, Haidee Head and Sophie McQueen, who have all been ruled out with injury.

Rugby.title: England forward Packer to miss North America tour
Rugby.summary: Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.
Rugby.body:
Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States. The Harlequins back-rower will remain in the United Kingdom with her partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth.

England face Canada on 17 and 24 October (both 00:00 BST starts) before playing the USA in one-off match on 30 October (21:15 BST). England are boosted by the return of Kelsey Clifford for the North American tour, with the Saracens prop returning from a hamstring injury.

Rugby.title: Springboks great Francois Steyn set to call Swansea home
Rugby.summary: The Toyota Cheetahs will make Ospreys’ St Helen’s their European home this season after striking an agreement to stage their EPCR Challenge Cup pool fixtures in Swansea.
Rugby.body:
The Toyota Cheetahs will make Ospreys’ St Helen’s their European home this season after striking an agreement to stage their EPCR Challenge Cup pool fixtures in Swansea. The South African side, coached by Springboks great Francois Steyn, will face Dragons at the ground on December 13 before returning to take on Top 14 outfit Perpignan on January 17.

Both matches will form part of double-header weekends at St Helen’s. The Ospreys host Harlequins 24 hours before the Cheetahs meet the Dragons, while Vannes visit Swansea the day before the Cheetahs face Perpignan.

Rugby.title: Cheetahs to play European games in Swansea
Rugby.summary: South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys.
Rugby.body:
South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys. Cheetahs host Dragons on Sunday, 13 December and Perpignan on Sunday, 17 January with both games a day after Ospreys' home matches in the same competition.

Cheetahs have traditionally used Europe as a base for matches in the second-tier tournament, with games in the 2025-26 season taking place in Amsterdam. There are links between Ospreys and Cheetahs. Y11 Sports & Media owns a majority stake in the Ospreys and maintain an investment interest in the South African team with players moving between both sides.

Rugby.title: Toulon statement: Head coach Pierre Mignoni quits with immediate effect
Rugby.summary: Pierre Mignoni has stepped down from his role as Toulon head coach with immediate effect following a poor start to the Top 14 season which sees the side languishing in 13th place.
Rugby.body:
Pierre Mignoni has stepped down from his role as Toulon head coach with immediate effect following a poor start to the Top 14 season which sees the side languishing in 13th place.

The three-time European champions have only won one of their opening five matches of the campaign, against newcomers and bottom-place Vannes, and suffered a 28-0 defeat to Montpellier on Sunday.

Rugby.title: Sudamérica Rugby gives Rugby World Cup 2035 bid update
Rugby.summary: South America's top rugby-playing countries, led by Argentina, have released a statement saying they have officially submitted all the information required by World Rugby to be considered as a candidate to host Rugby World Cup 2035.
Rugby.body:
South America’s top rugby-playing countries, led by Argentina, have released a statement saying they have officially submitted all the information required by World Rugby to be considered as a candidate to host Rugby World Cup 2035.

World Rugby launched the selection process for RWC 2035 at their General Assembly in London just over 12 months ago, and several countries have stepped forward. The preliminary hosting bid process includes the submission of documentation, visits to the candidate venues, and the announcement of the preferred venues in May 2027. The final decision will be made by the World Rugby Council in November 2027

Rugby.title: Quins display one of worst I have ever seen
Rugby.summary: Ugo Monye calls former club Harlequins' 48-0 defeat by Gloucester "one of the worst performances I have ever seen".
Rugby.body:
Former Harlequins winger Ugo Monye has called the club's 48-0 defeat by Gloucester on Saturday "one of the worst performances I have ever seen". Quins conceded eight tries in their heaviest league defeat for 26 years and are bottom of the early Gallagher Prem table.

"They got smashed in the scrum and the line-out. Their backfield coverage was poor. They got smashed at the gain line," Monye said on the Rugby Union Weekly podcast. "They didn't score a single point in a league where they're literally handing out points for free [this season]."

Rugby.title: Tana Umaga: 'You can definitely see the stamp of Les Kiss on this Wallabies side'
Rugby.summary: The changes Kiss has made have borne fruit, and All Blacks defence coach Tana Umaga was quick to put his finger on exactly where they've come when speaking with media after training on Tuesday.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks are looking forward to facing a familiar foe with a similar attacking mindset when the Bledisloe Cup kicks off in Auckland this weekend, but their rivals from across the ditch have some new quirks to their game that demand defensive adjustments.

The Kiwis aren’t the only side introducing a new head coach’s game plan this year, with Les Kiss the new kid on the Wallabies’ block. Wins over Japan, Argentina and South Africa have got Kiss’ tenure off to a flying start just one year out from a home Rugby World Cup, and there would be no better way to affirm that momentum than not only ending a more than two-decade-long Bledisloe Cup drought, but also New Zealand’s three-decade-long unbeaten run at Eden Park.

Rugby.title: ‘Sticks in the guts’: Tana Umaga on defensive response required against Wallabies
Rugby.summary: "It's probably the one stat we look at the most: the three in the red that we lost," the former Moana Pasifika head coach said in Auckland on Tuesday.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks defence coach and former captain Tana Umaga has urged his side to bounce back against the Wallabies at Eden Park, after slumping to three straight defeats against the Springboks.

Umaga, who was appointed by All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie as the team’s defence coach, admitted in Auckland on Tuesday that he’s not sure an All Blacks side in his lifetime has ever lost three Tests on the trot while conceding an average of 35 points.

Rugby.title: ‘Australia are hitting a sweet spot of Test experience; it’s exciting to think where they could get to over the next 12 months’
Rugby.summary: With RWC 2027 just under a year away, Australia fans are daring to dream about what sort of shape their team might be in by then.
Rugby.body:
There’s a train of thought among rugby aficionados, commentators and pundits, that somewhere in the vicinity of 25 to 40 Tests of experience represents something of a sweet spot for players building their international careers.

The thinking is that once inside this range, players know more about the requirements of the top level of the game and how they need to prepare for it, they’re probably less inclined to make the kind of errors under pressure or fatigue that might easily be put down to inexperience, and they’re no longer a risky decision at the selection table.

Rugby.title: Saracens management letting players down
Rugby.summary: Former England scrum-half Danny Care says "some of the powers that be" at Saracens have "let the players down".
Rugby.body:
Former England scrum-half Danny Care says "some of the powers that be" at Saracens have "let the players down" after a turbulent start to the season. An opening weekend 40-38 win at Leicester was followed by a 21-17 home defeat by Sale, the build-up to which was marred by headlines made by returning director of rugby Brendan Venter.

He reportedly refused to perform a series of media obligations, putting Saracens at risk of fines amid conjecture his job title had been changed to 'head of rugby culture and wine consultant', although the club have since clarified he is now head of culture and technical director.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly
Rugby.summary: Ugo, Ashy and Danny raise a glass and dissect round two of the Prem season.
Rugby.body: Ugo, Ashy and Danny raise a glass to Brendan Venter’s short stint as Saracens’ wine consultant and review round two of the Prem. Venter finally spoke to the media, but was it worth the wait? And has the whole saga damaged the club’s reputation? The West Country clubs continued their 100% start to the season. Louis Rees-Zammit is back on the wing and scoring tries as Bristol put 41 points on champions Northampton, Gloucester schooled Quins at Kingsholm and Bath dug deep to edge another thriller with Exeter at The Rec. We also talk Sir Kev, Bristol’s new approach to post-match media and hear about Ashy’s trip up north.

Rugby.title: 'Gloucester deserves a top rugby team playing at the top of the league'
Rugby.summary: Winless after their first two games last season, and sat eighth in the table, Gloucester have flipped the script this term and breezed past Exeter 45-24 and Harlequins 48-0.
Rugby.body:
After two bonus point wins from two, Gloucester are sitting pretty at the top of the Gallagher PREM table, ahead of West Country rivals Bristol and Bath on points difference. It may be early days, but the turnaround at Kingsholm is quickly becoming one of the early storylines of the season.

Winless after their first two games last season, and sat eighth in the table, Gloucester have flipped the script this term and breezed past Exeter 45-24 and Harlequins 48-0. It is the first time since the start of the 2007/08 season, the year they finished the regular season in first place but lost in the semi-finals of the playoffs to an Andy Goode drop goal, that the Cherry & Whites have looked down on the rest of the PREM two matches in.

Rugby.title: Cardiff try machine Tom Bowen happy for the 'small' wins
Rugby.summary: He scored a brace of tries in last Friday’s 47-27 bonus point victory over Zebre Parma at the Arms Park, taking his tally to 13 from 21 appearances in all competitions for the club.
Rugby.body:
Try machine Tom Bowen has a simple message for all smaller players in the game: “Back yourself”. At 5ft 7ins and 11st 11lbs, the Cardiff Rugby winger is dwarfed by some of the giants on the circuit, but he is standing tall with his performances.

He scored a brace of tries in last Friday’s 47-27 bonus point victory over Zebre Parma at the Arms Park, taking his tally to 13 from 21 appearances in all competitions for the club.

Rugby.title: Big Ireland win sees Wales benefit in World Rugby rankings
Rugby.summary: Ireland's 43-19 victory over Japan in Cork has seen Wales return to 11th in the World Rugby rankings.
Rugby.body:
Ireland’s 43-19 victory over Japan in Cork has seen Wales return to 11th in the World Rugby rankings. On Saturday afternoon, Eilis Cahill, Brittany Hogan, Neve Jones, Anna McGann, Beibhinn Parsons, Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett all crossed the whitewash at Virgin Media Park to rack up an impressive win.

The victory means that Ireland have now won two of their three fixtures so far this autumn. Their most recent fixture against Japan took place out of the WXV Global Series window, just one week after they beat the Sakura Fifteen 31-24 in Galway.

Rugby.title: ‘We wanted to disrupt their attack’: Springbok Women finish tour with Spain shutout
Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women ended their European tour on Sunday with a 20-0 win over Spain in Seville.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women ended their European tour on Sunday with a 20-0 win over Spain in Seville. A WXV Global Series crossover fixture against Regis Sonnes’ Las Leonas, who finished third in the 2026 WXV Global Series Challenger, saw South Africa claim their second win of the tour.

In Seville, Catha Jacobs finished off a sensational scrum move to open the scoring after 14 minutes. Jakkie Cilliers converted the try before adding three more points from the tee in the 30th minute to give the visitors a 10-0 half-time lead.

Rugby.title: Metcalfe back in Wales WXV reckoning for Japan
Rugby.summary: Nel Metcalfe is in a 30-strong party that will be led by co-captains Alex Callender and Kate Williams for back-to-back Tests in Japan.
Rugby.body:
Full-back Nel Metcalfe has a chance to resurrect her Wales career after being named in Sean Lynn's squad for their WXV double-header against Japan. The 21-year-old Gloucester-Hartpury player has fully recovered from the knee injury that ruled her out of the 2026 Women's Six Nations.

Lynn named Metcalfe in his extended training squad for the stunning WXV win against South Africa and subsequent defeat by the United States, but she did not make the matchday squads.

Rugby.title: ‘There’s a bigger score out there’: Ireland boss demands more after Japan win
Rugby.summary: Scott Bemand believed that Ireland left points out on the pitch after their 43-19 win against Japan on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand believes his side could have scored 50 or even 60 points against Japan despite their 43-19 victory in Cork on Saturday. The out-of-window Test at Virgin Media Park saw Ireland run in seven tries, although Japan threatened a comeback in the second half before the hosts pulled away late on.

The Sakura Fifteen took an early lead when Sakurako Korai bundled over in the fourth minute, but Ireland responded with four tries in the following 36 minutes from Eilis Cahill, Brittany Hogan, Neve Jones and Anna McGann.

Rugby.title: Salty celebrations, questionable signings and Test bolters
Rugby.summary: Bristol set out their top-four aspirations with a statement win, while Gloucester's renaissance continues in the second round of Prem action.
Rugby.body:
The stats piled up after a car-crash performance by Harlequins in a 48-0 shellacking by Gloucester. The biggest league defeat in 26 years. Seventeen penalties conceded. Only two entries made into the opposition 22m. Not one of their starting forward pack making more than four carries.

It was a desperately under-powered display. Boss Jason Gilmore described it as "totally unacceptable" in the aftermath. The Australian has overseen a few eyesores during his time in charge; a 38-0 reverse at Sandy Park and a 40-14 reverse at the club's festive fixture at Allianz Stadium come to mind.

Rugby.title: Nel Metcalfe returns to Wales squad for Japan WXV tour
Rugby.summary: Wales boss Sean Lynn has named a 30-player squad to tour Japan in October as part of WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Wales boss Sean Lynn has named a 30-player squad to tour Japan in October as part of WXV Global Series. Nel Metcalfe, who missed the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations with injury, has returned to the squad. The Gloucester Hartpury full-back has not turned out for Wales since the team’s loss to Fiji at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

The squad will continue to be co-captained by back-row pair Alex Callender and Kate Williams. Uncapped prop forwards Stella Orrin and Crystal James have been named in the squad.

Rugby.title: Golden Finish in Nagoya for Hong Kong China Men and Japan Women
Rugby.summary: Golden Finish in Nagoya for Hong Kong China Men and Japan Women asiarugby.com
Rugby.body:
Hong Kong China claimed the men’s gold medal and Japan secured the women’s title as rugby sevens at the Aichi–Nagoya 2026 Asian Games concluded in front of a capacity crowd at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Rugby Field on Saturday, 3 October.

Hong Kong China defeated China in the men’s final to secure their third consecutive Asian Games gold medal, following titles in Jakarta in 2018 and Hangzhou in 2023. Hong Kong China reached the final by defeating Korea, while China edged hosts Japan in a closely contested semi-final. Japan recovered to claim the men’s bronze medal, completing the podium alongside Hong Kong China and China.

Rugby.title: 'I could skip homework if I went to rugby training': Marius Simionescu, the reluctant player who became Romania's kingpin
Rugby.summary: Rugby bored the full-back as a teenager, but he was persuaded to stick at the game, and now a key man for Romania, cannot imagine life without it.
Rugby.body:
Goosebumps. There’s no other way to describe listening to Marius Simionescu, a beacon of the Romania team, map out his rugby journey. The full-back talks with burning passion about what the game has given him, as he left home and familiarity behind to chase his dreams and represent his country.

The 29-year-old was born in the town of Erbiceni and raised mostly in Ia?i, a region in the far eastern corner of Romania. His parents moved to Italy to earn a better living for their family and Simionescu spent much of his childhood under the care of his grandmother. He was 14 when rugby found him, persuaded by renowned Romanian coach Gabriel Popa to join a local team.

The 29-year-old was born in the town of Erbiceni and raised mostly in Ia?i, a region in the far eastern corner of Romania. His parents moved to Italy to earn a better living for their family and Simionescu spent much of his childhood under the care of his grandmother. He was 14 when rugby found him, persuaded by renowned Romanian coach Gabriel Popa to join a local team.

They recorded a second successive bonus point victory by beating defending champions Leinster Rugby 26-20 at Kings Park on Saturday evening. The Player of the Match award went to their winger Edwill van der Merwe who secured both the win and a bonus with a try two minutes from time.

Rugby.body:
Former England No.8 Nathan Hughes capped his call-up to Fiji’s squad by bagging a try in his first appearance of the Top 14 season for Racing 92 on Saturday. The 35-year-old came off the bench in Racing’s 55-25 victory over Perpignan, making an immediate impact just days after being included in the Flying Fijians’ 68-man extended squad.

Hughes, who won 22 caps for England between 2016 and 2019, missed out on Fiji’s Nations Championship squad in July but is now back in the frame ahead of the Test against Japan on October 24 and the Nations Championship fixtures that follow.

Rugby.summary: Allan Alaalatoa believes the visitors can take confidence and belief from their preparation into the fixture.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies are under no illusions about the challenge that awaits at the All Blacks’ Eden Park fortress this weekend, but Allan Alaalatoa believes the visitors can take confidence and belief from their preparation into the fixture.

Alaalatoa made his 39th appearance in the gold jersey when the Wallabies last defeated the All Blacks on November 7, 2020. The now 94-Test prop remains a regular starter for the Wallabies, who come into the Bledisloe Cup series on a six-game unbeaten run.

Rugby.title: The biggest handbrake on the Wallabies’ momentum ahead of their Bledisloe Cup bid
Rugby.summary: On the surface, the Wallabies seem to have all the right cards to enter the Bledisloe Cup race with confidence and momentum, but the closing of the Regulation 9 window, injuries, and suspensions will mean the bad type of selection headaches for Kiss and his assistants.
Rugby.body:
Rugby Regulation 9 window is now closed. Regulation 9, which provides official release windows for overseas players to return to their national sides, is not in effect for the Bledisloe Cup series in October, and it means the Wallabies are without two of their best and most impactful forwards, Taniela Tupou and Tom Hooper, for the two toughest matches of 2026.

There’s no two ways about it: the Tests against the second-best team in the world, the All Blacks, are the two hardest matches the Wallabies will play all year. Not only will the All Blacks be desperate to retain the Bledisloe Cup after a disappointing Greatest Rivalry Tour, but they won’t be fielding a heavily rotated side as the Boks did in Perth.

Rugby.summary: Billionaire Roosters boss teases big signing after two grand final wins Nine.com.au
Rugby.body:
A cross-code star is set to make her way to the Sydney Roosters NRLW team next year, in a move that is only going to make the premiership winners even stronger. In the aftermath of the club winning the men’s and women’s premierships, the club’s chairman Nick Politis could not hide his joy about the Roosters’ success.

The 85-year-old billionaire was seen walking along the sidelines interacting with the club’s fans when he was brought in for a chat with Nine’s Brad Fittler. Politis said it was “so good and unbelievable” that they club won two premierships, but he was more impressed by how dominant the teams had been in recent years.

Rugby.title: Sale Sharks player ratings vs Saracens | 2026/27 Gallagher PREM
Rugby.summary: Eight days removed from a frustrating home loss to open the season, Alex Sanderson's Sale Sharks pulled off the rarest of away wins at the Stone-X to down Saracens 21 - 17.
Rugby.body:
Eight days removed from a frustrating home loss to open the season, Alex Sanderson’s Sale Sharks pulled off the rarest of away wins at the Stone-X to down Saracens 21 – 17. Built on a foundation of defensive belligerence, the Sharks led by Tom Curry, Joe Marchant and Courtney Lawes battered the Saracens attack. Stunting any really opportunities to get flow into their attack, the Sharks overcame a two man deficit to limit Saracens to just five points at half-time.

Coming out of the blocks quickly in the second half through a moment of magic by Tom O’Flaherty, the visitors had their tails up. A try by Sione Va’enuku brought the home side back to within a score three minutes later but as had been the case all afternoon, Sanderson’s side responded through Ben Bamber in the 65th minute.

Rugby.title: Sale defy Jacques Vermeulen’s first-half red card to beat Saracens
Rugby.summary: Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen’s first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O’Flaherty emerging as the star of a slug fest at StoneX Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen’s first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O’Flaherty emerging as the star of a slug fest at StoneX Stadium. Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.

Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O’Flaherty produced the match’s pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try. It was part of a dominant second half from Sale, who capitalised on the hosts’ lifeless performance to bounce back after losing to Bristol on the opening weekend with their hooker Nathan Jibulu also outstanding.

Rugby.title: History made in Top 14 as longstanding record falls to Pumas fly-half
Rugby.summary: Twice retired 40-year-old Pumas fly-half Benjamín Urdapilleta made Top 14 history on Saturday after nailing his second of three kicks in USA Perpignan's match against Racing 92.
Rugby.body:
Twice retired 40-year-old Pumas fly-half Benjamín Urdapilleta made Top 14 history on Saturday after nailing his second of three kicks in USA Perpignan’s match against Racing 92.

Heading into the match, the former Pumas international had recorded 2,611 points in the Top 14, just a couple behind Romain Teulet in the professional era. The fly-half then matched Teulet’s record after converting Braydon Ennor’s try, then added two more successful penalty kicks, setting the new record at 2,619.

Rugby.title: 'A great sign'
Rugby.summary: Leicester head coach Geoff Parling believes there is still “loads to improve on” following their 24-19 win over Newcastle at Kingston Park.
Rugby.body:
Leicester head coach Geoff Parling believes there is still “loads to improve on” following their 24-19 win over Newcastle at Kingston Park. The hosts went ahead through Obi Ene, but Leicester regained control and claimed a 17-5 lead at the break as Samiuela Moli and Adam Radwan both crossed and Billy Searle kicked a penalty.

A closely-fought second half saw George McGuigan score for Newcastle before Will Hurd charged over from a close-range tap and go to extend the Tigers’ advantage. However, the visitors were forced to hang on toward the end as Cam Jordan went over and Parling revealed there were mixed feelings in the changing room post-match.

Rugby.title: Oliver Smith's double helps Australia U18 rally to beat NZ Schools in thriller
Rugby.summary: Both sides attacked ferociously in the opening stages, but it was New Zealand that were offered the first real opportunity of the contest.
Rugby.body:
Australia U18 have come up clutch against New Zealand Schools, beating the hosts 40-33 at St Paul’s Collegiate in Hamilton, in an end-to-end battle. Dale Roberson’s side, clearly the most impressive team at the tournament, came from behind to overpower the Kiwis in Hamilton. Despite the home side leading 19-12 at the break, Australia burst out of the blocks after halftime to stun New Zealand Schools on Sunday evening.

The first half was a thrilling contest filled with lead changes and big moments, with both sets of captains coming up with huge plays on both sides of the ball. The home side, coached by New Zealand Pathways coach Kane Jury, looked the more threatening with ball in hand, but the Australian defence held strong on several occasions.

Rugby.title: Trying to style Henry Pollock into a rugby icon is missing something
Rugby.summary: This Pollock stuff is about Pollock. It’s not about Northampton or England. It’s not even about rugby. It’s about a promoter deciding, seemingly on a whim, that this is a person of substance that we’re going to be told is transformational so many times.
Rugby.body:
If this is where rugby is going, it might be a journey it takes without me. Rugby, to me, is the ultimate team game. Tall or short, big or small, there’s always been a place for you.

It’s not about individuals, but the collective. If you’re modest, hardworking and brave you’ll earn the respect of everyone. No-one’s bigger than the team, no-one says or does stupid things that put a target on people’s heads. You talk a small game, but play a big one.

Rugby.title: The URC talking points as Wales hopefuls impress
Rugby.summary: Which players are impressing as Cardiff and Dragons enjoy strong starts in the United Rugby Championship while Scarlets and Ospreys are still hunting a win.
Rugby.body:
Only two rounds of the United Rugby Championship (URC) have been completed but it is Cardiff and Dragons who are the early Welsh pacesetters, while Scarlets and Ospreys are languishing at the bottom of the table in 14th and 15th respectively.

Cardiff have won both games and lie second, while Dragons in sixth are unbeaten after winning an entertaining 10-try derby against Scarlets in Newport. Ospreys and Scarlets are battling for long-term survival, with only one west Wales side set to exist in two years, but currently they would love just a victory after two defeats each.

Rugby.body:
Bristol boss Pat Lam hailed Louis Rees-Zammit’s “lethal” quality after he inspired the Bears’ 41-26 victory over Gallagher Prem champions Northampton at Ashton Gate. The Wales wing followed up his two tries against opening Prem opponents Sale Sharks with another double as Bristol triumphed in bonus-point fashion.

“He is sharp, you know, and he loves finishing,” Lam said. “We know that if we can give him time and space, he is lethal. He is back on the wing (Rees-Zammit made appearances at full-back for club and country last season), and most importantly that is where he wants to be.”

Rugby.body:
Gloucester continued their impressive start to the Gallagher Prem season by handing out a 48-0 thrashing to hapless Harlequins at Kingsholm. The eight-try win followed up their impressive opening day victory over Exeter at Sandy Park – but that success was far more meritorious as Harlequins were incredibly poor on the day.

Rugby.title: Glasgow and Ulster play out thrilling draw in URC
Rugby.summary: George Horne's late penalty hits the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster play out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship.
Rugby.body:
George Horne's late penalty hit the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster played out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship. Ulster, seeking their first win in Glasgow in more than five years, led 19-14 at the break but the Warriors scored three tries in a clinical nine-minute spell when Ulster had two players sin-binned to take the lead.

But Glasgow were reduced to 13 inside the final 10 minutes and Juarno Augustus' try, converted by Nathan Doak, levelled the game. Despite being two players down, Horne had a chance to win the match but his penalty came back off the upright with four minutes left and the points were shared at Scotstoun.

Ireland recovered from conceding an early try to cross the whitewash four times in the first half to help them to a 22-7 advantage at the break. Rugby.title: HK men’s Rugby Sevens claim historic hat-trick of Asian Games titles with shutout victory
Rugby.summary: HK men’s Rugby Sevens claim historic hat-trick of Asian Games titles with shutout victory thestandard.com.hk
Rugby.body:
Hong Kong’s men’s rugby sevens team has written a glorious new chapter in the city's sporting history by successfully defending their Asian Games gold medal in Nagoya, defeating the national team with a commanding 26-0 shutout.

This triumphant victory secures an unprecedented third consecutive Asian Games crown for the squad, while simultaneously elevating Hong Kong's gold medal haul at these Games to an all-time high of 11. The historic gold also takes the city's overall medal tally to 54, officially breaking the previous record set at the Hangzhou Games.

Rugby.title: Asian Games: city’s men make it hat-trick of rugby sevens golds, women win bronze
Rugby.summary: Asian Games: city’s men make it hat-trick of rugby sevens golds, women win bronze South China Morning Post
Rugby.body:
There are very few certainties in life, although Hong Kong’s men winning rugby sevens gold at the Asian Games could well be one of them. A 26-0 win over China on Saturday sealed a third consecutive title for the city’s team at the Games, and it is now 12 years since they last lost a match at the multi-sport event.

Their mainland opponents had already been beaten 22-0 in a Pool A game on Friday, and a first-half double from Harry Sayers ended any threat of an upset. Bryn Phillips added a third, and converted all three as well, ensuring there was no way back for China. With little need to press the issue in the second half, the only additional score came seconds after the restart, with Juan Esono Mba Oyana crossing in the corner.

Rugby.title: Pietsch, Charlie star as Western Force power to Super Rugby AUS title
Rugby.summary: 363 days on from the heartbreak of a narrow defeat in the inaugural Super Rugby AUS Grand Final, the Western Force have gone one better.
Rugby.body:
363 days on from the heartbreak of a narrow defeat in the inaugural Super Rugby AUS Grand Final, the Western Force have gone one better by overcoming defending champions the NSW Waratahs 53-26 at Perth’s Scotch College.

Winger Dylan Pietsch, 95-Test Wallaby Kurtley Beale and Australia Sevens representative Wallace Charlie all impressed as the Force ran away with an emphatic result. It’s a drought-breaking title for the Force, with the men’s team last claiming silverware in the 2019 Global Rapid Rugby and National Rugby Championship. The Force made the playoffs two years later in Super Rugby AU but the wait for another title went on.

Rugby.summary: Bulls lock Reinhardt Ludwig is starting to attract serious interest from Japan Rugby League One outfits despite being tied down at Loftus Versfeld until the summer of 2028.
Rugby.body:
Bulls lock Reinhardt Ludwig is starting to attract serious interest from Japan Rugby League One outfits despite being tied down at Loftus Versfeld until the summer of 2028. Ludwig, 24, who also plays at blindside flanker, made his Bulls debut in a defeat against the Stormers in January 2021 and started the new season on fire, scoring two tries and winning 10 lineouts in the win in Zebre.

Japanese clubs are taking a close look at the former Baby Bok, a Junior World Cup winner five years ago, who has forced his way back into Johan Ackermann’s plans after seven months in the wilderness following Ruan Nortje’s departure.

Rugby.summary: Former Maori All Blacks captain Kurt Eklund has announced his sudden retirement from rugby due to a neck injury.
Rugby.body:
Former Maori All Blacks captain Kurt Eklund has announced his sudden retirement from rugby due to a neck injury. The 82-cap Blues hooker, who hasn’t featured on the field since round 14 of the Super Rugby Pacific season, made the announcement ahead of Bay of Plenty’s final game of the NPC round-robin.

Eklund, 34, was a key figure in the Blues’ all-conquering 2024 season, earning him an All Blacks XV call-up and further Maori All Blacks honours before he assumed captaincy of the latter team in 2025.

Counties Manukau will hold onto the prized Ranfurly Shield until next year after surviving a tense finish to beat Hawke’s Bay 12-7 in the National Provincial Championship, despite not scoring any points beyond the 27-minute mark.

Rugby.body:
The men’s and women’s rugby sevens teams of the Sports Federation & Olympic Committee of Hong Kong, China have advanced from pool play at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026. Both teams are hoping to repeat podium finishes from 2022. Hong Kong China’s men’s team are two-time defending gold medalists, while the women won the city’s first ever rugby sevens women’s medal with bronze in Hangzhou, China.

It didn't happen in the first phase or second phase, like what we had in the previous games, so I thought we managed that game particularly well.

Rugby.body:
Bath beat Exeter Chiefs 40-34 in a pulsating West Country derby at the Rec to take them to the top of the Gallagher Prem table but they were made to fight all the way in an 11-try thriller.

Cam Redpath, Dan du Preez, Bernard van der Linde, Ted Hill and Finn Russell scored Bath’s tries. There was also a penalty try award with Russell converting four.

Rugby.summary: Gloucester winger Phil Cokanasiga is ruled out until January after undergoing surgery on a foot injury suffered against Exeter.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester winger Phil Cokanasiga has been ruled out until January after undergoing surgery on a foot injury suffered in the win against Exeter. The 25-year-old played the entire 80 minutes of the impressive 45-24 victory at Sandy Park but head coach George Skivington told BBC Radio Gloucestershire - before the extent of the injury was known - that he "caught his foot" towards the end of the game.

Cokanasiga joined the Cherry and Whites this summer from United Rugby Championship side Ospreys and scored two tries on his debut in the Prem Rugby Cup defeat by Bristol earlier this month.

Rugby.title: Saracens exile was 'bewildering', says returning Lozowski
Rugby.summary: Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was an anti-climax after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign.
Rugby.body:
Sale centre Alex Lozowski says the end of his decade-long stint at Saracens was "sad" and "bewildering" after being reduced to a fringe player for his farewell campaign. The 33-year-old England international made only two Prem appearances for Saracens last season, with a 10-minute Champions Cup cameo off the bench his only game time since the end of February.

"It was a sad ending for everyone I suppose," said Lozowski. "They finished fifth, which is not where they wanted to be, and I wasn't part of it at all. "It was probably just a bit of a damp squib at the end of the season really, which was a shame. It was bewildering and peculiar to me.

Rugby.summary: Georgia, Spain, Romania, and Portugal have signed a Memorandum of Understanding and established the IV Nations Alliance, an initiative focused on shared sustainable growth and a more ambitious future.
Rugby.body:
Georgia, Spain, Romania, and Portugal have signed a memorandum of understanding and established the IV Nations Alliance, an initiative focused on shared sustainable growth and a more ambitious future.

Rugby.title: Injured stars hope for Christmas miracles as URC rivals smell Irish blood in the water
Rugby.summary: With two key Ireland players on the sidelines and all four provinces losing their opening URC games, the league's most dominant country is on the back foot.
Rugby.body:
As World Rugby marked a one-year countdown to Australia hosting the 2027 World Cup, a host of Ireland stars were named in their first squads of the season. Sam Prendergast, Ciarán Frawley, Craig Casey, Robbie Henshaw, Cormac Izuchukwu, Tom Clarkson, Cian Prendergast and Rónan Kelleher will launch into their seasons this weekend. There will be highs, lows, injuries, axings, accolades, analysis sessions, dropped balls and stuffed mauls in between, but all will hope to do enough to make it to the start line Down Under next year.

Two players decidedly out of the spotlight for a significant chunk of those 12 months are key to Ireland’s World Cup cause. Leinster and Ireland captain Caelan Doris will not return until early 2027. The 28-year-old broke his foot at the tail-end of last season – missing summer Test matches for the second year running. Doris had surgery on that busted foot over the summer, and also had a procedure carried out on his knee. There have been complications with his rehabilitation timeline, according to The Irish Times, caused by an infection picked up in that repaired knee. Leinster are sharing around the captaincy until he returns, with Dan Sheehan likeliest to lead Ireland when the Nations Championship re-opens for business in November.

Rugby.summary: As the Sharks prepare to take on the Irish powerhouse Leinster this Saturday at Kings Park in the United Rugby Championship, attention will inevitably shift from the players on the field to the coaching staff.
Rugby.body:
As the Sharks gear up to face the formidable Leinster this Saturday at Kings Park during Round Two of the URC, the spotlight will inevitably shift from the athletes on the pitch to the strategic minds guiding them.

At the forefront is Leinster’s senior coach, Jacques Nienaber, who will find himself under keen scrutiny. Sharks’ defence coach, Joey Mongalo, has chosen to approach the idea of a personal rivalry with caution, referring to Nienaber as “the godfather of defence.”

Rugby.title: Wade closes in on record as tries dominate Prem
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade sits four away from Chris Ashton's all-time record of 101 as tries dominate Prem Rugby.
Rugby.body:
The opening week of the new Prem season was all about tries, tries, tries as the league's 10 teams went on all-out attack. No fewer than 52 tries were scored across the five matches, setting a record for the opening round of a season, with an average of more than 10 per game and four players claiming hat-tricks as spectators were royally entertained.

Contributing two of those scores was Christian Wade for Newcastle Red Bulls in their 59-26 loss at Northampton Saints, as the veteran winger moves closer to an all-time record.

Rugby.title: Report: Early TV viewing figures for PREM add to upbeat mood
Rugby.summary: Across four metered televised matches, the cumulative audience on TNT Sports was more than double that of 2025/26: over 795,000, compared with 390,000 last year.
Rugby.body:
TV viewing figures for round one of the new Gallagher PREM season are double what they were at this stage of the competition last year. Entertainment may mean different things to different people, but it seems armchair fans are buying into the high-scoring fare on offer. The 52 tries scored last weekend are a record for the opening round of the 30-season old competition, which for the last four seasons, has only involved 10 teams as opposed to anything between 11 and 14 in the past.

As reported by Andy Milnes of Neisen Sports, across four metered televised matches, the cumulative audience on TNT Sports was over 795,000, compared with 390,000 last year. Those numbers do not include non-metered coverage of Bath’s 33-17 win over between Harlequins on the opening night, which was carried on TNT Sports 5.

Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga is expecting to face a Wallabies team full of confidence when the All Blacks host their trans-Tasman rivals at Eden Park next weekend.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga is expecting to face a Wallabies team full of confidence when the All Blacks host their trans-Tasman rivals at Eden Park next weekend. Mo’unga, who has faced the Wallabies a dozen times in his All Blacks career, commended the men from across the ditch for their hard-fought win over the Springboks last weekend as he laid out his expectations for the coming Bledisloe Cup series.

The 42-38 victory was the fifth straight win to begin Les Kiss’ time at the helm of the one-time world champions, and Mo’unga expects it will have put a spring in their step coming into the famed annual series.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has ended months of speculation about his career, confirming his “last dance” in Super Rugby Pacific will be with the Blues. Savea teased the announcement for about 40 minutes on a YouTube livestream, before making the move official on Instagram.

Savea played more than 130 Super Rugby matches for the Hurricanes before heading overseas to Japan with the Kobe Kobelco Steelers. The backrower returned to Super Rugby Pacific in 2025 with Moana Pasifika and was named the competition’s Player of the Year.

Rugby.body:
Wales wing Josh Adams says he would love to play in a third World Cup as he targets a first trip to Australia next year. It is exactly a year until Wales play their opening game against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October, before further pool games against Tonga and England.

"I'm desperate to go, but there is loads of rugby to be played and months ahead of us," said Adams, looking ahead to the tournament. "It is important that you navigate your way through correctly and get to that start line in a good spot to be selected."

Rugby.summary: Coach Les Kiss has named a 34-man Wallabies squad that’s bracing for a “formidable challenge” across the ditch.
Rugby.body:
Coach Les Kiss has named a 34-man Wallabies squad that’s bracing for a “formidable challenge” across the ditch, as the All Blacks look to avoid a couple of unwanted feats at their long-standing Eden Park fortress in Auckland.

France were the last team to taste victory over New Zealand at the venue, claiming a three-point win on July 3, 1994. The All Blacks returned to the Garden a month later, starting their still-standing unbeaten run by drawing 18-all with the Springboks.

Rugby.body:

The Ireland international was Connacht’s marquee signing of the summer following his move from Leinster, a move that left many blue supporters, and indeed Leo Cullen, disappointed to see him depart.

Viewed as a move that could benefit both player and country, the 28-year-old’s switch to Galway should bring more game time at fly-half and help establish him as a genuine long-term Ireland No.10 option for Andy Farrell.

Overall, they have claimed 162 wins in North v South matches, compared with 94 northern wins. They began the new season by recording a clean sweep of victories in the opening round of matches, three of the four being bonus point wins.

Rugby.summary: After two years in French fields, Curwin Bosch is back on South African soil and already receiving rave reviews.
Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Wales counting down the year until World Cup
Rugby.summary: With one year to go before the 2027 Rugby World Cup, what lies in wait for Steve Tandy's Wales over the next 12 months before they head to Australia?
Rugby.body:
It might be hard to believe how quickly it comes around, but Thursday marks a year to go until the men's Rugby World Cup begins in Australia. The 2027 competition starts on 1 October in Perth with a match between Australia and Hong Kong China, with the tournament finale on 13 November in Sydney.

Wales are to feature in the second game when they open their campaign against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October. Steve Tandy's side sit 11th in the world rankings, currently topped by reigning World Cup champions South Africa.

Rugby.body:
Three weeks after leading South Africa to their ‘Greatest Rivalry’ series-clinching win over New Zealand in Baltimore, double World Cup-winning captain Siya Kolisi will make his second Stormers debut against Edinburgh at The Hive Stadium on Friday.

Kolisi played 118 games for the Cape Town outfit between 2012 and 2020 before two spells at the Sharks, either side of an underwhelming stint with Racing 92 in Paris. The Springbok captain will start at openside flank in what will be his first appearance for the Stormers in six years, following his return to Cape Town.

Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears have suffered a major blow ahead of Saturday evening’s visit from Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints, as England and Lions loosehead Ellis Genge will miss the game with a wrist injury.
Rugby.body:
Bristol Bears have suffered a major blow ahead of Saturday evening’s visit from Gallagher PREM champions Northampton Saints, as England and Lions loosehead Ellis Genge will miss the game with a wrist injury.

Genge sustained the injury in the opening minute of the 34-24 win over Sale Sharks in the season opener and played on for more than an hour before asking to be taken off. Bears boss Pat Lam believes Genge, who was playing his first game of the season after an extended rest following international duty in the summer, will be out for only two to three weeks at most.

Rugby.title: Harlequins back row Chisholm retires aged 31
Rugby.summary: Harlequins back row James Chisholm retires from professional rugby union aged 31, almost two years after rupturing his Achilles.
Rugby.body:
Harlequins back row James Chisholm has retired from professional rugby union aged 31. Chisholm said his recovery from a ruptured Achilles in January 2025 had been "a bit of an uphill battle" and "unfortunately my body just can't get there".

"I still have the want to play and was really looking forward to this season and gave pre-season my all. We tried everything but I just couldn't get there," he told club media., external

Rugby.title: Two former players at Melrose’s Greenyards added to Scotland rugby sevens squad
Rugby.summary: Two former players at Melrose’s Greenyards added to Scotland rugby sevens squad The Southern Reporter
Rugby.body:
Two former players at Melrose’s Greenyards have been added to Scotland’s rugby sevens squad. Ex-Southern Knight Freddie Owsley and erstwhile Melrose winger Ross McCann are among four new faces taken on by Borderer Ciaran Beattie’s now-seven-strong full-time contracted squad, the others being Ben Salmon and Lewis Wells.

Their arrival takes the number of ex-Greenyards players in the squad to four as they join another former Knight, Jacob Henry, and prior Melrose scrum-half Roan Frostwick. Henry and Frostwick, both 26, have been kept on from last season’s squad of six, together with Matt Davidson.

Rugby.summary: Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu will play his first match of the new season in Glasgow’s home URC clash with Ulster at Scotstoun on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu will play his first match of the new season in Glasgow’s home URC clash with Ulster at Scotstoun on Saturday. The talismanic centre, who faces a big year ahead leading into the 2027 Rugby World Cup, will have his workload carefully managed across the coming campaign.

But having sat out Warriors’ opening win over Munster in Limerick, Tuipulotu returns this week in one of three changes to the starting XV with Stafford McDowall, who continues to captain the side, switching to outside centre to accommodate Tuipulotu and Ollie Smith dropping out of the 23.

Rugby.title: Isiekwe available after Leicester red rescinded
Rugby.summary: Nick Isiekwe's red card in Saracens' Prem victory at Leicester is rescinded at a disciplinary hearing, meaning he will be available for Sunday's match against Sale.
Rugby.body:
Nick Isiekwe's red card in Saracens' Prem victory at Leicester on Saturday has been rescinded at a disciplinary hearing. The England forward, 28, was shown a 20-minute red card following a high tackle on Tigers full-back Freddie Steward in Sarries' 40-38 win.

Steward provided a statement and live evidence at the hearing, in which he said he did not suspect any foul play by Isiekwe. Steward and Isiekwe both described the head contact as "glancing", a term that the independent panel said it "did not fully accept", although the panel's view was that the degree of force was "low to mid and not high".

Rugby.summary: Back-rower Ben Muncaster faces a fresh spell on the sidelines as emerging prop Ollie Blyth-Lafferty is handed the chances to press his Scotland claims.
Rugby.body:
The latest injury misfortune to strike the luckless Ben Muncaster will see the Edinburgh back-rower sidelined for 10 weeks, ruling him out of Scotland’s November series of Nations Championship matches.

Muncaster is to undergo surgery on ankle damage he suffered in his comeback outing a fortnight ago in Edinburgh’s final pre-season game against Harlequins. The 24-year-old Scotland cap will miss at least the capital club’s next five games leading into the international window, starting with Friday’s home URC clash with Stormers, and is unlikely to return to action until December.

Rugby.title: Munster statement: CEO Ian Flanagan to step down
Rugby.summary: Munster have confirmed that chief executive Ian Flanagan will step down from his role at the end of October, bringing his tenure at the province to a close.
Rugby.body:
Munster have confirmed that chief executive Ian Flanagan will step down from his role at the end of October, bringing his tenure at the province to a close. Flanagan, who was appointed to the role in 2019, has informed the Munster Rugby Board of his decision, with the IRFU and province announcing that an interim CEO will be appointed in the coming weeks.

A recruitment process for a permanent successor will then begin, leaving Munster with another off-field change as they move through the weeks of the new season. Flanagan’s time in charge included a central role in the development and delivery of Munster’s €7.3m Centre of Excellence in Cork, a long-term investment in player development and the wider game across the province.

Rugby.title: One-cap England star Charlie Atkinson decides PREM club future
Rugby.summary: Gloucester have confirmed that Charlie Atkinson has signed a new contract that will keep him at Kingsholm until at least 2029.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester have confirmed that Charlie Atkinson has signed a new contract that will keep him at Kingsholm until at least 2029. The 24-year-old fly-half joined the Cherry and Whites in early 2024 and has since established himself as their first choice fly-half, seeing off the challenge of ex-Ireland international Ross Byrne, who was signed in 2025.

Atkinson enjoyed a standout 2025/26 campaign, sweeping Gloucester’s end-of-season awards after being named Coaches’, Players’ and Supporters’ Player of the Season. His form has also been recognised internationally. The former Oxford RFC player has made six England A appearances and earned his first senior England cap against the USA in 2025.

Rugby.title: ‘The gap’s getting bigger’: The changing face of English rugby
Rugby.summary: Six Nations titles, low-scoring games and former rugby league players: three things that have seemingly vanished from men's rugby union in England.
Rugby.body:
Six Nations titles, low-scoring games and former rugby league players: three things that have seemingly vanished from men’s rugby union in England. England’s Six Nations struggles and the Gallagher PREM’s increasingly basketball-like scorelines have been well documented, but the disappearance of rugby league converts has happened far more quietly.

In the 2000s, four former league players represented England in rugby union, with Jason Robinson the poster boy. Seven followed in the 2010s. So far this decade, there have been none.

Rugby.title: ‘The RWC countdown clock is ticking. The permutations are endlessly fascinating. England are in a critical phase.’
Rugby.summary: South Africa are in that good place again, a potential Wallabies resurgence is on the cards but England's form has been variable.
Rugby.body:
England supporters must feel like Butch Cassidy as they look at their team and wonder, “Who are those guys?” Butch eventually did find out when the pursuing posse closed in while Sundance chided his pal in typically laconic fashion: “That’s your trouble. You’re always thinking”.

So, who are Steve Borthwick’s guys – the lot who won 12 matches on the spin not so long ago or the mob who flunked the 2026 Six Nations, thumped by Ireland at home and beaten by Italy for the first time ever? Or even the gallant, up-and-at-‘em outfit that did at least close that dreadfully disappointing championship with a gutsy performance against France?

Rugby.summary: The RFU and Exeter Chiefs have confirmed that Sandy Park will host England A's fixture against an Ireland XV on February 20, 2027.
Rugby.body:
The RFU and Exeter Chiefs have confirmed that Sandy Park will host England A’s fixture against an Ireland XV on February 20, 2027. Mark Mapletoft’s side will head to Devon during the 2027 Guinness Six Nations, with the fixture taking place a week before England A face Chile at Kingsholm in Gloucester.

While it has hosted many England Women’s games in recent years, the match will be the first men’s England A representative fixture at Sandy Park since 2012, when England Saxons defeated the Irish Wolfhounds 23-17.

Rugby.title: Hector Patterson: 'I hear stories about Gary Armstrong
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh's impressive and assertive young scrum-half hails from the Borders heartlands and is primed for a breakout campaign.
Rugby.body:
For 50 blistering minutes, Edinburgh ran Ulster into the Affidea plastic. The ambition and accuracy, the verve and the tempo, and the supreme levels of fitness required to deliver it, had not been seen from this side in an age. Edinburgh scored belter after breathtaking belter, and though they almost succumbed to a very Edinburgh-like capitulation late on, the hope is, victory heralds a new dawn for a club which has lain stagnant far too long.

Watching Edinburgh these past few seasons has typically been as exciting as filling in a tax return. It raised your blood pressure, yes, but probably not your pulse. In one glorious hour, the formulaic, turgid fare of old melted away under the Belfast floodlights.

Rugby.title: Simon Middleton: Why Lesley McKenzie and Shaun Edwards can transform their new teams
Rugby.summary: Ex-Red Roses boss Simon Middleton muses about Lesley McKenzie's move to coach Os Lobos and Shaun Edwards' arrival in England camp.
Rugby.body:
The first thing is that I think Lesley McKenzie is one of the best infielders at her craft, particularly in the contact area or the contact defensive area. This isn’t to say she isn’t very strong in other areas; she is a well-rounded coach, but every coach specialises in one thing. In Lesley McKenzie’s case, that is contact. Personally, I’ve never seen or worked with a better contact coach than her – whether in the women’s or men’s game.

But don’t take my word for it; take Dean Benton’s [former head of sport science for England Rugby and Director of Rugby Melbourne Storm] or Ollie Richards’ [acclaimed S&C coach, specialising in MMA fighting], as they both could attest to the same.

Rugby.title: A comprehensive guide to the 2026 World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup
Rugby.summary: 2026 will mark the debut of the newly established World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup, with eight nations from all over the world meeting in Chile to fight for a chance to claim the title.
Rugby.body:
2026 will mark the debut of the newly established World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup, with eight nations from all over the world meeting in Chile to fight for a chance to claim the title.

Chile will host Portugal, Romania, Hong Kong China, Brazil, Canada, Belgium and Namibia over the next fifteen days, with the competition’s first kick-off set for this Friday. The tournament is split into two groups of four teams: Brazil, Chile, Romania, and Hong Kong China in Group A, and Portugal, Canada, Namibia, and Belgium in Group B. All matches will be played at CARR Parque Mahuida in Santiago, Chile; the first round is scheduled for October 2, the second for October 7, and the third for October 12, followed by the finals on October 17, where each group winner will compete for the chance to be named champions.

Rugby.title: Rugby World Cup 2027 marks one year to go with ticket sales milestone
Rugby.summary: “In just 365 days, Australia will welcome the world for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027, a landmark tournament that coincides with the competition's 40th anniversary and promises to be the biggest and most accessible celebration of rugby ever staged.
Rugby.body:
It’s officially one year until Rugby’s pinnacle tournament, the Rugby World Cup, with World Rugby celebrating a special ticketing milestone for the tournament, which will be held in Australia between October 1 and 13 November 2027.

1.3 million tickets have already been purchased by supporters from 164 countries, showcasing the global want and anticipation for the eleventh edition of the Rugby World Cup. Out of the tickets purchased with over a year to go until the marquee tournament, 51 per cent of the people are aged between 16 and 44.

Rugby.title: Hunter Paisami learns fate after late yellow card against Springboks
Rugby.summary: "The Disciplinary Committee has found Australian midfielder Hunter Paisami guilty of dangerous play for a contrary tackle, in breach of Law 9.13.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies will be without powerful Reds No.12 Hunter Paisami for the 2026 Bledisloe Cup series after receiving a six-week ban for a high shot in the 78th minute against the Springboks.

The 28-year-old has been handed a six-game ban but will miss four Test matches, with the disciplinary committee adding a two-game reduction due to his recent disciplinary record and other mitigating factors.

Rugby.summary: Hall will join the defending Super Rugby Pacific champions in their 2027 title defence, which kicks off on Saturday, February 13 against the Blues in Auckland.
Rugby.body:
The Hurricanes have called upon six-time Super Rugby Pacific champion Bryn Hall to back up Cameron Roigard for the 2027 season, signing the former Crusaders and Blues halfback on a one-year deal.

Hall, who has played 123 Super Rugby appearances, returns to the competition following a stint with the Shizuoka Blue Revs and the Kubota Spears. Rugby.summary: Influential Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson signs a new contract to stay at Kingsholm until the summer of 2029.
Rugby.body:
Influential Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson has signed a new contract to stay at Kingsholm until the summer of 2029. The 24-year-old, who won an England cap against the United States last year, was voted the Cherry and Whites' player of the season by players, fans and coaches last season.

Atkinson moved to Gloucester from Leicester Tigers in December 2024 and has gone on to play 57 times for the club in all competitions. As well as his one England appearance he has also been a regular in England's A side, playing three times for them last season.

Rugby.title: Leinster and Ireland reportedly dealt Caelan Doris hammerblow
Rugby.summary: Leinster and Ireland have suffered another setback, with captain Caelan Doris expected to remain sidelined until at least the new year after complications have delayed his recovery from surgery, The Irish Times have reported.
Rugby.body:
Leinster and Ireland have suffered another setback, with captain Caelan Doris expected to remain sidelined until at least the new year after complications have delayed his recovery from surgery, The Irish Times have reported.

The No. 8 injured his foot during Leinster’s United Rugby Championship final victory over the Bulls in June and underwent surgery, with a knee procedure also carried out. His rehabilitation has since been slowed by an infection in the knee, pushing his anticipated return beyond the Nations Championship in November.

Rugby.title: Morgan and Lake lead the charge across the Severn Bridge as Welsh influence grows
Rugby.summary: Gloucester's star summer signings inspired their new club to a fantastic 45-24 win over last season's finalists Exeter Chiefs.
Rugby.body:
The Gallagher PREM feels more Welsh than at any point in its 30-season history, even in the two seasons that London Welsh were in the top division in England. Sure, plenty of Welsh players have played in the PREM in the past – the Bath front-row pair, Jon Humphreys and Paul James, used to car share for the commute over the Severn Bridge, while northern clubs Sale and Leeds often looked that way in their recruitment. But not in the same quantity, or quality, as now.

Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, who’ve captained their country within the past 12 months, were two of the headline acts of the summer transfer activity, swapping Ospreys for Gloucester.

Rugby.title: France forced to find new captain for New Zealand tour
Rugby.summary: France captain Pauline Bourdon Sansus will not travel to New Zealand for her team's WXV Global Series fixtures against the Black Ferns.
Rugby.body:
France captain Pauline Bourdon Sansus will not travel to New Zealand for her team’s WXV Global Series fixtures against the Black Ferns. In agreement with the coaching staff led by François Ratier, the scrum-half will remain in France for family reasons. She remains available to join the squad if required. A new captain will be announced on Wednesday 7 October.

Bourdon Sansus’ absence means France will turn to a new captain for their tour of New Zealand. With regular skipper Manae Feleu unavailable this autumn as she prioritises her medical studies, Ratier will have to select his latest leader carefully.

Rugby.title: Tom Curry extends Sale Sharks contract
Rugby.summary: England international flanker Tom Curry signs a two-year contract extension with Sale Sharks.
Rugby.body:
England international flanker Tom Curry has signed a two-year contract extension with Sale Sharks. The 28-year-old has spent his entire career with the Sharks and made his debut aged 18 in October 2016 and his new deal will keep him with the Prem side until the end of the 2027-28 campaign.

Director of rugby Alex Sanderson said Curry, whose identical twin brother Ben also plays for the club, is "fundamental" to the team. "The terms are a couple of years and that's on Tom's desire to ensure that he's physically in the best spot to be able to honour his contract, to play a load of games for the next two years," Sanderson said.

Rugby.title: Matt Ferguson exits Harlequins to take up Red Roses role
Rugby.summary: Matt Ferguson has left his role with PREM Rugby club Harlequins to take up a role with the RFU as a scrum and contact skills coach.
Rugby.body:
Matt Ferguson has left his role with PREM Rugby club Harlequins to take up a role with the RFU as a scrum and contact skills coach. The former Northampton Saints scrum coach will work with John Mitchell’s Red Roses and in the women’s pathway system. In a previous stint with the RFU, Ferguson was the Red Roses’ forwards coach for three years and contributed to the team’s run to the 2017 Women’s Rugby World Cup final.

Ferguson is credited with converting Sarah Bern from a back-row to tighthead prop. He then spent seven seasons with Northampton Saints between 2018 and 2025, in which time a number of the East Midlanders’ tight five forwards gained Test honours, before he joined Harlequins as lead rugby transition coach.

Rugby.title: Claire Thomas column: The Red Roses are learning to win without winning
Rugby.summary: It’s a cliché - but, these days, you don’t lose: you learn.
Rugby.body:
It’s a cliché – but, these days, you don’t lose: you learn. Defeats are simply an opportunity to get better, and experiences only wasted if they don’t lead to forward motion. If evolution is the outcome, then don’t sweat the process, and it’s no bad thing to snap a win streak if it galvanises the next one. Capiche?

If we’re going with that, then Red Roses – Canada ending in a dead heat was the *perfect* result for the world champions. Their unbeaten run – phew – rumbles on, but 26-26 delivered quite the wake-up call, and forced England to plumb depths which had grown, frankly, dusty.

Rugby.summary: Altron Document Solutions Backs SA’s 2026 Deaf Rugby Sevens Team SA Good News

Rugby.body:
Having had a first taste of playing for Wales, Ryan Woodman now wants more as he beefs up and looks to get physical. The Dragons RFC flanker came on as a replacement in the uncapped international against the Barbarians at Twickenham in June.

That saw him packing down alongside Jac Morgan, Aaron Wainwright and Dewi Lake, while going up against the likes of Faf de Klerk, George Norge and Virimi Vakatawa. Now he is aiming to press his claims for inclusion in the squad for the Nations Championship which will be named in three weeks time, with an eye on making his Test debut.

Rugby.title: Has the balance between attack and defence become too lopsided?
Rugby.summary: There was a record amount of tries on the opening weekend of the Gallagher Prem, but has it got out of hand?
Rugby.body:
Who would want to be a defence coach right now? The opening weekend of the Prem delivered a record 52 tries, the chaotic Australia v South Africa classic in Perth nine more. Rugby union’s ever-evolving balance between attack and defence has never been so strongly weighted in favour of the former.

Whether this is a good thing or not depends on your standpoint. Professional rugby is in the entertainment business and a try is its crowd-on-feet, adrenaline-spike moment. Plenty of tries equals plenty of excitement.

Rugby.summary: France international Sekou Macalou has pushed back against reports that he has retired from professional rugby with immediate effect, insisting that any announcement about his future will come from him.
Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Pirates focused on putting heavy loss behind them
Rugby.summary: Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are focused on putting their 73-40 loss at Coventry behind them.
Rugby.body:
Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are focused on putting their 73-40 loss at Coventry behind them. Coventry scored 11 tries as Pirates suffered one of their heaviest defeats in a Champ fixture.

The loss came a week after an impressive opening weekend win over Doncaster at the Mennaye Field. "The boys are motivated, you don't become a bad team overnight," Cattle told BBC Radio Cornwall.

Rugby.title: 'Lions Women can learn from darts and 1997'
Rugby.summary: Whitney Hansen and Jo Yapp, coaches of New Zealand Women and the British and Irish Lions Women respectively, sit down for joint interview with Rugby Union Weekly
Rugby.body:
A year to go until the inaugural Lions Women's tour and two of the biggest names in the game are having their first ever face-to-face meeting in a hotel in Shepperton. Lions Women's head coach Jo Yapp and New Zealand Women's head coach Whitney Hansen will become the first female coaches to lead two of the best sides in the professional era.

"One of my hopes is that everyone in the rugby world remembers where they were when it took place" explains Hansen. "It's Spiderman isn't it – with great power comes great responsibility."

Rugby.title: Ireland to host England at Aviva Stadium in Six Nations
Rugby.summary: Ireland's 2027 Women's Six Nations encounter with England will be played at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.
Rugby.body:
Ireland's 2027 Women's Six Nations encounter with England will be played at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin. Scott Bemand's side made their Six Nations debut at the Aviva Stadium with a win over Scotland in this year's competition and will welcome the world champions to Dublin in the fourth round of fixtures on 8 May.

A crowd of 31,294 watched the 54-5 win over Scotland in May, a record crowd for a women's match in Ireland. "Playing at Aviva Stadium last season was an incredible and landmark experience for the group and we're really excited to be returning to the home of Irish rugby in 2027," said Ireland captain Erin King.

Rugby.title: Ireland confirm Aviva Stadium return for 2027 Women's Six Nations
Rugby.summary: Ireland will host England at Dublin's Aviva Stadium in a blockbuster Round 4 of the 2027 Guinness Women's Six Nations.
Rugby.body:
Ireland will host England at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium in a blockbuster Round 4 of the 2027 Guinness Women’s Six Nations. Earlier this year, Scott Bemand’s team played their first-ever standalone fixture at the venue against Scotland and welcomed a record crowd of 31,294 to the venue. At the same Championship, the world champion Red Roses hosted Ireland at Allianz Stadium and saw a crowd of 77,120 make its way to West London.

It has also been confirmed that Ireland’s Round 2 fixture against France will be hosted at Galway’s Dexcom Stadium. Last weekend, Ireland beat Japan 31-24 at the venue and got their first win of WXV Global Series 2026.

Rugby.title: Tickets go on sale for historic first British & Irish Lions Women tour
Rugby.summary: Tickets for Test fixtures at next year's first-ever British & Irish Lions Women tour in New Zealand have gone on sale.
Rugby.body:
Tickets for the inaugural British & Irish Lions Women’s Tour of New Zealand have gone on sale. In September 2027 the inaugural British & Irish Lions Women squad, comprised of the best players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales will take on the Black Ferns in three Tests in New Zealand.

For a limited time, Test matches taking place in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch will have selected children’s tickets priced at NZD$1 and adult tickets cost NZD$27. The first Test will take place at Auckland’s Mount Smart Stadium, then Wellington Memorial Stadium a week later and the series will conclude at Te Kaha in Christchurch. Tour fixtures against the Black Ferns XV and the Invitational XV will take place in Whangarei and Hamilton.
