Rugby.title: Iosefa-Scott set for France move when contract ends
Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says prop Josh Iosefa-Scott is likely to move to France when his contract ends next summer.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter says prop Josh Iosefa-Scott is likely move to France when his contract ends next summer. Reports in France have linked the 30-year-old tight-head with a move to Provence after six seasons at Sandy Park.

The English-qualified New Zealander has played 99 games in all competitions for the Chiefs since moving from Waikato in the summer of 2021. "I haven't had any confirmation of whatever club he's going to," Baxter told BBC Sport of the prop, whose current deal runs out in the summer.

Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson says that it would be a disaster for the Gallagher PREM if England lifted its ban on selecting overseas-based players for national duty.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson says that it would be a disaster for the Gallagher PREM if England lifted its ban on selecting overseas-based players for national duty. Toulouse flanker Willis, 29, last played for England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup after being granted dispensation to represent his country while playing his club rugby in France following Wasps’ collapse.

Rugby.title: ‘Complete package’: O’Mahony has no hesitation in Erasmus vs Farrell call
Rugby.summary: Peter O’Mahony has picked Andy Farrell over Rassie Erasmus as the best coach he worked under, despite offering a glowing assessment of the Springbok boss’ coaching ability.
Rugby.body:
Peter O’Mahony has picked Andy Farrell over Rassie Erasmus as the best coach he worked under, despite offering a glowing assessment of the Springbok boss’ coaching ability. The former Ireland and Munster captain was speaking on the For the Love of Rugby podcast following the release of his book All In, having worked closely with both Farrell and Erasmus during his career.

While Erasmus initially arrived at Munster in more of an overarching director of rugby role, O’Mahony explained that the South African was also an accomplished hands-on coach when circumstances required him to take a greater role on the training field following the death of Anthony Foley.

Rugby.title: 'The Wallabies moved several steps closer to cracking the Springboks' DNA code'
Rugby.summary: Australia picked up where New Zealand left off in unearthing more of the tools which could stop South Africa's charge for a third straight Rugby World Cup.
Rugby.body:
The fictional scientists in the 1993 blockbuster Jurrasic Park use frog DNA to gap-fill broken dinosaur code extracted from prehistoric mosquitoes and fabricate their very own version of the real thing. If there is a complete DNA strand of ‘how to beat the world champions at rugby’ waiting to be discovered somewhere deep underground, frozen in amber, nobody has yet unearthed it. The All Blacks found some parts in the recent Greatest Rivalry series, the Wallabies dug up rather more at the weekend. But nobody yet has the complete code, despite Australia’s nail-biting 42-38 victory at the Optus Stadium in Perth.

There is no doubt the science is moving closer to finding an answer, and the pack are gaining ground on the Springboks. The idea there are two or even three potential South African teams waiting in the wings to bring home ‘Bill’ for a World Cup-winning three-peat next year was thoroughly exposed as the fiction it truly is.

Rugby.title: England's Underhill to miss autumn internationals
Rugby.summary: England and Bath flanker Sam Underhill is out for months with a ruptured biceps that requires surgery.
Rugby.body:
England flanker Sam Underhill will miss the Nations Championship this autumn after rupturing his biceps in Bath's opening Prem game away at Harlequins. Underhill went off in the 48th minute of the win at The Stoop and was seen at the end of the game with strapping around his arm, which will require surgery later this week.

Bath expect the 30-year-old to be out until December or January, meaning he will miss a large portion of the domestic season as well as England's three internationals against Australia, Japan and New Zealand in November.

Rugby.summary: Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral.
Rugby.body:
Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral. Sheedy headed the ball forward after chasing his own kick in the second half of the 21-15 victory against Scarlets on Saturday night.

The clip has had more than 800,000 hits across social media. "I probably wasn't thinking at the time, that was the problem," said Sheedy. "I remember the ball sitting up, and I could see Blair [Murray] coming towards me, and I thought it was going be an aerial contest.

Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints boss Phil Dowson has delivered a positive injury update on Italian winger Edoardo Todaro, who is now back in training and likely to be available for selection in the next couple of weeks.

Rugby.title: Ex-Kelso and Gala fly-half Craig Dods named as head coach of Canada’s rugby sevens team
Rugby.summary: Ex-Kelso and Gala fly-half Craig Dods named as head coach of Canada’s rugby sevens team The Southern Reporter
Rugby.body:
Ex-Kelso and Gala fly-half Craig Dods has been appointed as head coach of Canada’s rugby sevens squad and as an assistant to their national XVs team. The 34-year-old, also a former development officer at the Poynder Park and Netherdale clubs, joins Rugby Canada after four years working for the Scottish Rugby Union as a specialist kicking coach.

“I’m delighted to be joining Rugby Canada at a pivotal time for the sport in such a proud and passionate rugby country,” said the Borderer, son of 23-times-capped Scotland full-back Peter Dods.

Rugby.summary: Former Australia U20 captain Toby Macpherson has been named in a Wallabies squad for the first time.
Rugby.body:
Former Australia U20 captain Toby Macpherson has been named in a Wallabies squad for the first time, selected as one of two uncapped players in the 34-man group for the upcoming Bledisloe Cup Series against the All Blacks.

Macpherson is coming off a breakout Super Rugby Pacific campaign for the ACT Brumbies, and the lock-backrow utility stepped up as the team’s captain during the three-round Super Rugby AUS regular season.

Rugby.summary: James O’Connor is among a host of internationally experienced players who are set to suit up for the Western Force in the Super Rugby AUS Grand Final.
Rugby.body:
James O’Connor is among a host of internationally experienced players who are set to suit up for the Western Force in the Super Rugby AUS Grand Final in Perth, as the home side looks to go one better after last season’s decider.

O’Connor has been named on the bench for the Force, joined in the 25-man matchday squad by capped Wallabies Tom Robertson, Kurtley Beale and Dylan Pietsch. Harry McLaughlin-Phillips was selected in the most recent Wallabies squad but remains an uncapped prospect.

Rugby.summary: NSW Waratahs coach Lachlan McCaffrey has made seven changes to the First XV that fell to the Western Force 17-12 last weekend.
Rugby.body:
NSW Waratahs coach Lachlan McCaffrey has made seven changes to the First XV that fell to the Western Force 17-12 last weekend, with scrum-half Teddy Wilson among the returnees for the Super Rugby AUS Grand Final in Perth.

Wilson was rested for the final-round match at Warringah Rugby Club, following a busy Super Rugby Pacific season and helping Easts take out the Shute Shield title. But the former Australia U20 captain is back in the mix, as the Tahs prepare to face the Force yet again.

Rugby.summary: Wallabies great Michael Hooper was impressed by Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii’s performance in the 42-38 win over the Springboks.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies great Michael Hooper was impressed by Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii’s performance in the 42-38 win over the Springboks, believing the utility was more influential in one start on the wing than in his last couple of appearances at centre.

Suaalii had only ever started at outside centre for the Wallabies, but coach Les Kiss made a huge selection call last week with the world champions in Australia. ‘Su’ joined Max Jorgensen and Tom Wright in a new-look back three, and they’re all able to make an impact.

Rugby.title: Jamal Ford-Robinson suffers cruel setback amid injury hell
Rugby.summary: Gloucester boss George Skivington has confirmed that Jamal Ford-Robinson’s injury hell continues after he needed another operation, this time on a hamstring injury he suffered in a training game against Bristol Bears.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester boss George Skivington has confirmed that Jamal Ford-Robinson’s injury hell continues after he needed another operation, this time on a hamstring injury he suffered in a training game against Bristol Bears.

Ford-Robinson, 33, who operates on both sides of the front row, only played four games last season between two dates with the surgeon’s knife for knee injuries, and his last game for the Cherry and Whites came in the defeat at Newcastle Red Bulls on January 2.

Rugby.title: Son of Scotland Grand Slam hero joins Canadian coaching staff
Rugby.summary: Craig Dods has left Scottish Rugby to join Rugby Canada's coaching setup as head coach of Canada's men's sevens team and assistant coach of the men's 15s team.
Rugby.body:
Craig Dods has left Scottish Rugby to join Rugby Canada’s coaching setup as head coach of Canada’s men’s sevens team and assistant coach of the men’s 15s team. The son of Peter Dods, a mainstay of the great Scotland 1984 Grand Slam-winning team and a British and Irish Lions tourist, was chosen from a long list of 70 applicants.

He comes into the role after serving as Scottish Rugby’s specialist skills coach, GB7s assistant coach and as a national talent pathway coach for Scottish Rugby. Previously, he has worked for Gala and Kelso in the Scottish Borders, as well as heading up Hungary’s women’s rugby programme for a couple of years,leading them to their best-ever finish on the Rugby Europe Sevens circuit.

Rugby.title: Saracens face fines over 'wine consultant' Venter's media no-shows
Rugby.summary: Saracens are facing fines from Prem Rugby for director of rugby Brendan Venter's failure to fulfil media commitments.
Rugby.body:
Saracens are set to receive a series of fines from Prem Rugby due to director of rugby Brendan Venter's failure to fulfil media commitments. It is understood the club have already been handed a £5,000 sanction after Venter was not present at the Prem's pre-season launch day.

The South African also did not speak to the media before, during or after the opening-weekend victory at Leicester. The Daily Telegraph reported earlier on Tuesday, external that Venter "resigned" as director of rugby last month and took up a new role of "head of rugby culture and wine consultant", with head coach Joe Shaw assuming responsibility for media commitments.

Rugby.title: Xoliswa Khuzwayo: Springbok Women embrace their ‘underdog’ status
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women prop Xoliswa Khuzwayo has admitted that her team don't mind being called the "underdogs".
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women prop Xoliswa Khuzwayo has admitted that her team don’t mind being called the “underdogs”. It has now been a year since South Africa stunned the world with their run to the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-finals and established themselves as a team to watch across the current World Cup cycle.

At the start of the year South Africa admitted that their aim is not to move further up the World Rugby rankings. Currently ranked 10th, the side have been challenged at WXV Global Series and started their autumn campaign with a loss to Wales in Cardiff, before they got back to winning ways with a 41-27 win against Italy in Pordenone.

Rugby.body:

Evans joined the club in 2020 and has been a key performer for the team in recent years. Capable of playing in the second row or back row, the 29-year-old made her 50th Test appearance for Wales last weekend against the USA Women’s Eagles in Cardiff.

Last season, she made 17 PWR appearances for the North London club as they won the English league title for the first time since 2022. Alex Austerberry, Director of Rugby, said: “Georgia is approaching 100 games for the club. This is testament to her quality as a player. Those appearances have come across the back five, which illustrates her versatility and ability to play in such abrasive and competitive positions at the highest level.

Rugby.title: Saracens bend the rules with bizarre Brendan Venter job title change
Rugby.summary: Saracens have responded to being fined for Brendan Venter's refusal to carry out media duties by changing his job title to “head of rugby culture and wine consultant”.
Rugby.body:
Saracens have responded to being fined for Brendan Venter’s refusal to carry out media duties by changing his job title to “head of rugby culture and wine consultant”. As Director of Rugby, the job title still given to him on Saracens’ official website, the South African is honour bound by PREM Rugby regulations to speak to the press.

However, Saracens say they asked the league’s organisers permission in July for head coach Shaw to be their designated media person. Shaw took Venter’s place at the pre-season content capture day at Allianz Stadium earler this month and has continued to fulfil those obligations, speaking to TNT Sports during their coverage of the London club’s impressive 40-38 victory at Mattioli Woods Welford Road on Sunday.

Rugby.summary: Five tries each, four yellow cards in the final 10 minutes and frayed nerves aplenty - relive the drama of Australia's win over South Africa.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have recorded the craziest win in living memory… feels like the sort of thing to say after that absolutely bonkers 42-38 win over South Africa in Perth on Sunday.

But then I had to check to see if I said the same thing after the Wallabies’ memorable 38-22 win at Ellis Park last August. I hadn’t, as it turned out, but Sunday still might only have been the craziest win in… well, a year.

Tennis.title: Calm in real life but demons on court
Tennis.summary: Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry - but his China Open disqualification was no surprise.
Tennis.body:
Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry. On court, though, he is a far more combustible character who finally ran out of chances when he was disqualified from Monday's China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Djokovic was serving for a place in the final when the ball ricocheted off the back of the court. Medvedev swiped it into the stands, where it hit a spectator in the face. A few minutes later the Russian was defaulted, as he had to be, under rules that bar a player from "hitting a ball dangerously or recklessly, or with negligent disregard of the consequences."

Tennis.title: Sabalenka stunned by Bartunkova at China Open

Tennis.body:
World number two Aryna Sabalenka followed Elena Rybakina out of the door at the China Open as she fell to a surprise defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova. It came a day after top seed Rybakina, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final and replaced the Belarusian at the top of the rankings, was knocked out by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.

Czech Bartunkova sprung another upset at the WTA 1,000 tournament and continued her breakthrough season with a 6-4 6-3 victory over Sabalenka. "I focused on myself, to be calm. She's a legend, so I'm really happy that I won the match," said 20-year-old Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next.

Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu Is Going to Drop Outside The Top 100 And Yet Her Ranking Tells the Wrong Story Yahoo Sports
Tennis.body:
I have been pretty harsh on Emma Raducanu over the years. Some of it, I still think, was more than justified. After all, I was hardly the only voice criticizing her choices. The coaching turnover became ridiculous at times. Some scheduling decisions were impossible to understand. Too often a promising run would be followed by another absence or another reset or another explanation for why the momentum had disappeared.

Five years after winning the US Open, that remains her only professional singles title. There has also occasionally been a tendency around Raducanu to treat perfectly normal progress as evidence that another New York miracle might be just around the corner. It usually wasn't.

Tennis.title: GB's Kartal wins on WTA return after six months out
Tennis.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal wins on her return to the WTA Tour after six months out with injury as she beats Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Sonay Kartal won on her return to the WTA Tour after almost six months out with injury as she beat Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open. The 24-year-old injured her lower back at Indian Wells in March and only made her return to tennis at the Billie Jean King Cup on 22 September.

Kartal, who narrowly lost to Czech world number 26 Marie Bouzkova on that return last week, produced a confident performance in Beijing to beat Spain's Lazaro Garcia 6-2 6-3. The Briton broke the qualifier's serve five times - helped by four double faults from her opponent - and landed 69% of her first serves.

Tennis.title: 'I kept fighting right to the end'
Tennis.summary: A tearful Kei Nishikori says he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ends his professional career at the Japan Open.
Tennis.body:
A tearful Kei Nishikori said he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ended his professional career at the Japan Open. Nishikori, known as one of the best players to never win a Grand Slam, lost 6-4 6-4 to world number eight Frances Tiafoe in Tokyo.

The 36-year-old became the first Japanese man to reach a major final when he faced Marin Cilic in the 2014 US Open showpiece. Nishikori beat then world number one Novak Djokovic on his way to the New York final and defeated Rafael Nadal for Olympic bronze at the 2016 Games in Rio.

Tennis.title: Navarro opens up on health struggles that caused 'deep anger' on court
Tennis.summary: American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" as she shares her long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.
Tennis.body:
American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" after opening up on long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.

Navarro, who claimed her first title in more than a year at the Strasbourg Open in May, is currently ranked 24th in the world. The 25-year-old was as high as eighth in 2024, the year she reached the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and Wimbledon, and the last four at the US Open in her native New York.

Tennis.title: Djokovic wins first match since Wimbledon in China
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic beats Nuno Borges at the China Open to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic maintained his remarkable unbeaten record at the China Open as he beat Nuno Borges to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July. The 39-year-old former world number one struggled in the second set but came through to win 6-3 7-6 (7-2) for his 30th consecutive victory in Beijing, albeit in his first appearance at the event since 2015.

Djokovic revealed in August that he has been dealing with an underlying health condition that causes particular issues in hot, humid conditions for "the past couple of years" and was far from his best against Portuguese Borges.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu drops in rankings again after pulling out of another event
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu drops in rankings again after pulling out of another event AOL.com
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has taken another hit in the rankings after withdrawing from the China Open due to a stress fracture in her right leg. The former US Open champion hasn't competed since making it to the Queen's Club final in June. The setback forced her to sit out Wimbledon and prevented a return to Flushing Meadows, where she made history with her Grand Slam victory in 2021.

Initially, Raducanu appeared on the entry list for the China Open, sparking optimism about her anticipated return in Beijing. Yet she was removed from the list weeks before the tennis event, suggesting her injury continues to linger. Her absence from competition has significantly impacted her WTA ranking, with the 23-year-old experiencing a dramatic decline.

Golf.title: LIV Golf gets $300M lifeline for 2027 relaunch after Saudi funding was pulled
Golf.summary: LIV Golf gets $300M lifeline for 2027 relaunch after Saudi funding was pulled lbc.co.uk
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has secured an initial funding commitment for a potential 300 million US dollars (£227m) investment from BC Partners Credit to help relaunch in 2027. The breakaway series filed for bankruptcy last month after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund – which had spent 5bn USD (£3.7bn) in four years – announced it was withdrawing support at the end of the season.

That cast the future of LIV into doubt but a deal with BC, subject to approval from the bankruptcy court, gives it the chance to reset next year. BC signed a term sheet with LIV last month, requiring it to sign half of the players to whom it owes money, as part of its financing plan.

Golf.title: LIV Golf makes HUGE announcement as 2027 deadline looms
Golf.summary: LIV Golf makes HUGE announcement as 2027 deadline looms Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has secured initial funding for its 2.0 era. In a statement released on Monday, BC Partners Credit announced an “initial committed investment in LIV Golf”. It added that it is the first part of a targeted $300 million in cumulative financing to help LIV Golf emerge from its restructuring as a fiscally strong, sustainable, team-focused golf league that complements the existing professional tours and contributes to the long-term potential of the sport”.

As part of the agreement, the deadline for players to commit to LIV’s future has been delayed. LIV filed for a Chapter 11 bankruptcy last month with claims that its ‘2.0’ era will be see the league become player-owned from 2027. CEO Scott O’Neil also promised to keep events “in places like Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong, and the United States”, as well as a field expansion to 75 players with a halfway cut and additional qualification pathways – including Monday qualifiers.

LIV Golf has secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season. The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, starting a court-supervised "restructuring process" that they hope to complete in early 2027.

It is unclear how much of the $300m LIV requires to start next year's schedule and which players will start the season. The competition's participants are owed at least $45m (£33m) and have the option to leave.

Golf.title: Former PGA Tour staple course finds new home as part of LPGA's new Hawaii swing
Golf.summary: The Plantation Course at Kapalua was a PGA Tour staple for 25 years. That relationship ended, but it now has a new one with the LPGA. The post Former PGA Tour staple course finds new home as part of LPGA’s new Hawaii swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Plantation Course at Kapalua was a PGA Tour staple for 25 years, hosting the Sentry, which served as the kickoff event from 1999 to 2013 and again from 2024 to 2025. That relationship ended in April when the PGA Tour announced it planned to end its tournament presence in Maui.

But while the PGA Tour won’t be returning to the Plantation Course next year, Kapalua now has a new professional golf partner in the LPGA. On Monday, the LPGA announced that the Lotte Championship will be hosted at the Plantation Course starting in 2027. The tournament, which Jeeno Thitikul won on Sunday, will now be held in March as part of a two-tournament Hawaii Swing along with the recently announced Nanea Cup. The Lotte Championship will have a $3 million purse next season.

Golf.title: TGL just signed golf's hottest young star. Here's why that matters
Golf.summary: Jackson Koivun to Motor City Golf Club might not have been on your offseason radar, but it's a significant move for TGL. Here's why. The post TGL just signed golf’s hottest young star. Here’s why that matters appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Jackson Koivun was always going to be 2027’s most anticipated young player. His professional arrival had been hotly anticipated for years, after all. There has long been a sense that the former World No. 1 amateur and Auburn standout is different, given his eye-popping collegiate resume, his knack for winning, his ability to embrace the biggest moments and bring his best, making him the kind of prospect with a high floor and a very, very high ceiling.

But he became an even bigger deal when he stared down Scottie Scheffler at the 3M Open, emerging as the winner in just his third start as a pro. And a bigger deal still when he was named to the U.S. Presidents Cup team, signaling his sky-high perception among his peers on Tour.

Golf.title: At Bank of Utah, the PGA Tour's different fall chases were on display
Golf.summary: Austin Smotherman won the day at the Bank of Utah Championship. but he wasn't the only winner of the PGA Tour's second fall event. The post At Bank of Utah, the PGA Tour’s different fall chases were on display appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Doug Ghim smiled as Austin Smotherman gazed into the Utah sky after winning his first PGA Tour event in 100 starts. There was no pain in Ghim’s face after his attempt to win his first title in 192 starts came up short. There was just gratitude that he’s still grinding and chasing his dreams on the top golf circuit in the world.

“It’s what we play for; it’s what we practice for,” Ghim said after finishing two shots behind Smotherman on Sunday at the Bank of Utah Championship. “Obviously the money and the points are great, but as a little kid trying to win a PGA Tour event, just a chance to do that is a dream come true. … We used to get really excited just to play courses that pros played at, and to think that as a 30-year-old, to have done this for my seventh season and to get an opportunity like today and what I’ve had in the past and hopefully more in the future, it’s such a privilege.

Golf.body:
While L.A.B. Golf’s usage on the PGA Tour has steadied somewhat from the momentum of a few years ago, it still doesn’t take long for any of their new putters to earn wins on the PGA Tour.

Case and point was Austin Smotherman’s win this weekend at the Bank of Utah Championship, wielding’s L.A.B.’s new VZN.1i (pronounced Vision One Eye) putter. The VZN.1i was released in June and is L.A.B.’s most forgiving design since the original Directed Force 2.1 putter. However, the main design characteristics are the strong visual cues that make the putter super easy to line up.

Golf.body:
Austin Smotherman finally broke through Sunday, winning his first PGA Tour title at the Bank of Utah Championship. Aside from deals with L.A.B. Golf for his putter and Titleist for the Pro V1x, Smotherman is a gear free agent, free to play whatever golf clubs he wants.

One of those clubs is a nearly seven-year-old TaylorMade SIM Max 3-hybrid, making him just the fourth player this season to win on the PGA Tour with a hybrid. The SIM Max rescue is one of the more famous TaylorMade hybrids of the past decade, mainly because it’s one of the last to get serious play on the PGA Tour.

Golf.title: The unauthorized blueprint to save U.S. golf's match play kryptonite
Golf.summary: The blueprint to saving American team golf already exists ... and it comes to us courtesy of a major Olympic sport. The post The unauthorized blueprint to save U.S. golf’s match play kryptonite appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you were to summarize the 2020s for American team golf, your words probably wouldn’t be very friendly. Well, unless you were a member of the team’s leadership, in which case your words to explain why the team has so frequently underwhelmed expectations might be a little too friendly.

E.g.: The conditions at Bethpage Black weren’t what the Americans expected … even though the team controlled the course setup. In Rome, a five-week layoff after the Tour Championship was too long for the team to stay sharp. And then there’s this one, also from Bethpage: Scottie Scheffler was sent out on the wrong set of holes in foursomes, forcing the World No. 1 to engineer a switch before his second alternate shot match of the weekend.

Golf.title: Austin Smotherman's Bank of Utah Championship win was a story 10 years in the making
Golf.summary: In his 100th career PGA Tour start, Austin Smotherman finally achieved a lifelong dream in Utah. It was a golf story 10 years in the making. The post Austin Smotherman’s Bank of Utah Championship win was a story 10 years in the making appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Back in March, Austin Smotherman entered Sunday at the Cognizant Championship on the precipice of his dream. Holding the 54-hole lead in a PGA Tour event for the first time in his career, the then-31-year-old faced the most terrifying round of his career. He navigated PGA National well enough that Sunday, but finished T2 as Nico Echavarria claimed the title after Shane Lowry imploded. But after he tapped in to close out his day, Smotherman looked like a man who had just won.

Because he knew that was a necessary step to get to where he eventually wanted to go. “This was kind of just my first really big pedestal,” Smotherman said that Sunday. “Kind of had a back door-ish top 5 in the Mexico Open at Vidanta a couple years ago, and never really had the same kind of moments coming down the stretch … This will be a week I always look back at.”

Golf.body:
Sunday night in the United States means it’s already Monday morning in Japan, and Titleist is getting a head start on what will surely be this week’s biggest gear story. This week’s Baycurrent Championship at Yokohama Country Club will officially launch Titleist’s new 2027 Pro V1 and Pro V1x golf balls.

The company is staying quiet on the technical details, which will come with the ball’s retail launch, likely in January or February if traditional launch cadences hold. The new golf balls first hit the USGA Conforming list three weeks ago at the Biltmore Championship, and several PGA Tour players have already made the switch. That was the result of a lengthy Tour feedback process by Titleist’s R&D team.

Golf.title: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews
Golf.summary: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: LIV Golf’s Adrian Meronk outlasts Casey Jarvis to claim victory at St Andrews Sky Sports
Golf.body:
Adrian Meronk came from four shots behind to overtake Casey Jarvis and win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two strokes on a gripping final day at St Andrews. The victory saw the LIV Golfer end a 1,078-day wait to claim his fifth DP World Tour title and regain his tour card for next season, as he wrapped up his week with a four-under 68.

Golf.copy:

Adrian Meronk’s professional career started at the Home of Golf, when he made his pro debut on the DP World Tour at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship in 2016. Golf.title: DP World Tour Warns LIV Golf Refugees About Returning
Golf.summary: DP World Tour Warns LIV Golf Refugees About Returning Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour has sent a clear message to LIV Golf players hoping to return after the breakaway league filed for bankruptcy. A tour spokesperson confirmed they see a surge in interest from players seeking a route back to Europe. However, any comeback requires meeting strict conditions. Players must be free of conflicting contracts and agree to follow existing membership rules. They might also lose access to the lucrative Rolex Series events. This stance comes as LIV Golf faces an uncertain future with its Chapter 11 filing in New Jersey.

Only 10 days remain for LIV players to determine whether they remain with the breakaway circuit or return to the DP World Tour or PGA Tour. The tour is exploring ways to accommodate these returning players, but it will not be automatic. Those who left for LIV before the bankruptcy are already facing hurdles. The tour granted conditional releases to eight members in February, including Tyrrell Hatton and Thomas Detry. These players agreed to pay fines and play extra tournaments to return without further punishment.

Golf.title: The key move that boosts swing speed — and the tool that can help train it
Golf.summary: Learn how the Why Golf Power Plate can help you improve your weight shift, boost ball contact and create more power in your swing. The post The key move that boosts swing speed — and the tool that can help train it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you’re looking for more speed and better contact, the answer isn’t just to swing harder. A big part of the equation is learning how to move pressure through your feet and into your lead side before impact. When that sequence is right, it becomes easier to deliver the club with a stable lower body, find the center of the face and compress the ball instead of catching it fat or thin. That’s the idea behind Why Golf’s Power Plate.

The training aid sets your feet on a slight incline, giving you an exaggerated feel for a proper weight shift in your swing. First, the incline makes it easier to shift your weight back into your trail leg. Then the goal is simple: move that pressure into your lead side without letting your body slide away from the target.

It all boils down to narrowing your focus.

Golf.title: Tom Kim's life-changing Asian Games win started with a message from Tiger Woods
Golf.summary: Tom Kim won gold at the Asian Games to earn an exemption from military service. His life-changing Saturday started with a message from Tiger. The post Tom Kim’s life-changing Asian Games win started with a message from Tiger Woods appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tom Kim’s last PGA Tour win, which came at the co-sanctioned Genesis Scottish Open in July, ended with a congratulatory text from Tiger Woods. On Saturday, as Kim prepared for a career-altering round at the 2026 Asian Games, Woods sent him a different message.

“Just be you. Nothing more, nothing less,” the message from Woods said, via Korea’s Yonhap News Agency. Kim arrived in Japan for this week’s Asian Games under immense pressure. South Korean men between the ages of 18 and 35 are required to serve up to 21 months in the defense forces. PGA Tour pros Sangmoon Bae and Seung-yul Noh served during their prime and it impacted their golf. But the South Korean government awards exemptions to athletes who win a gold medal at the Asian Games or any of the three medals at the Olympics. Si Woo Kim and Sunjae Im won a gold medal in the team competition at the 2023 Asian Games, earning an exemption from military service.

Golf.title: This talented mid-am is lovingly called 'Blandy.' Although he's anything but
Golf.summary: Andrew Davidson is lovingly called “Blandy.” But he’s anything but, and he’s one of the players in next week’s Bridges Cup. The post This talented mid-am is lovingly called ‘Blandy.’ Although he’s anything but appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Andrew Davidson does appreciate one view of his nickname. You don’t mind being called it in golf, because being it can be beautiful in golf. Basic pars are your friends. And a few years back, during one streak while at the University of Stirling, Davidson signed for them a lot.

He shot even par eight straight rounds, so of course his pals had to come up with something to call him other than “Andrew.” Thing is, though, it’s also a touch ironic. Golf.title: LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy Plan Relies On Player Equity Swap
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy Plan Relies On Player Equity Swap Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is filing for Chapter 11 protection after its Saudi backers cut off funding in April. The league owes millions in unpaid player salaries and legal fees. A new deal requires players to swap their unpaid cash for a majority ownership stake in the reorganized business. This move marks a desperate pivot from a cash-rich startup to a player-owned entity struggling to survive.

The financial math is stark. During the 90 days preceding bankruptcy, Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher received over $7.1 million from LIV Golf solely for legal fees. The firm agreed to discount its bills by 20% but still collected a massive sum. Meanwhile, the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, which spent over $5 billion trying to reshape pro golf, stopped writing checks. The league entered court with roughly $15 million in cash but faced a secured debt facility of approximately $495 million. That gap is too wide to bridge without a radical restructuring.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s In-House Lawyers Remain as Gibson Dunn Discounts Fees
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s In-House Lawyers Remain as Gibson Dunn Discounts Fees Bloomberg Law News
Golf.body:
LIV Golf Inc. paid more than $7.1 million to Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher in discounted legal fees as the once Saudi Arabian-backed professional golf circuit was shedding much of its workforce, according to bankruptcy court records.

LIV began laying off most of its employees in August, but almost all its in-house legal staff, including chief legal officer John Ruzich, have agreed to remain with the business through October, said three sources familiar with LIV’s operations. The company’s agreement with private equity firm BC Partners Advisors LP, which is backing LIV’s move to restructure through the Chapter 11 process, would require that at least 50% of its players convert their unpaid compensation into a majority equity stake in the reorganized business.

Golf.title: From Pine Valley to Trump Turnberry, golf keeps taking Andrew Price places
Golf.summary: For Team USA Bridges Cup competitor Andrew Price, golf has taken him to places he only used to dream about. The post From Pine Valley to Trump Turnberry, golf keeps taking Andrew Price places appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
For Andrew Price, the best part of golf might not be the pars and birdies — it’s where the game takes him. Price, 44, grew up in Lake Forest, Ill., playing just about every sport he could. Basketball, baseball and golf among them. By the time he reached high school, though, it was clear golf was the sport that would take him furthest. After a successful junior career, Price played collegiately at Kansas, competing for a top-25 program and building friendships that have lasted a lifetime.

But the real journey was just beginning. After college, Price spent a couple of years in Arizona before returning home to Chicagoland, where he eventually settled back in the suburbs, joining his family’s fourth-generation insurance business, leaving him time on the side to get his game in shape for amateur events. What started with events like the Western Amateur and USGA qualifiers gradually opened doors to the highest levels of mid-amateur golf. And with each new opportunity came another unforgettable experience.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia files to have LIV Golf contract terminated
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia files to have LIV Golf contract terminated RTE.ie
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia is pursuing the termination of his LIV Golf contract, a potential path out of the league. As LIV Golf works toward fulfilling a restructuring agreement following Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, Garcia's attorney argued in a six-page courtfiling on Wednesday that termination "should not be objectionable" to the league because it "is consistent with (LIV Golf's) statement that the agreement is 'not part of (LIV Golf's) go-forward business plan.'"

The Spaniard's camp further argued that with the contract still in place, "tournament organisers, sponsors and other counterparties may hesitate before dealing with Garcia, who may be unable to represent that they are free of competing contractual commitments".

Golf.body:
In the wake of the U.S. team’s thrilling comeback in Sunday singles to notch a 17-13 victory over the Internationals at the Presidents Cup, questions remain about the Americans’ performance in the team-match portion of the event — particularly in the foursomes format.

Foursomes — or alternate shot — has been difficult for the U.S. team in recent years. At this year’s Presidents Cup, the U.S. team went 2-7 in foursomes. And last year’s Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black was no better, with the U.S. going 2-6-0 against the Europeans.

Golf.body:
Here’s the truth about George Washington, the president who could not tell a lie: He left the country exactly once. That lone trip was to Barbados, where he spent six weeks in a house that bears his name today.

Washington was traveling with his half-brother Lawrence, who was seeking relief from tuberculosis. The island’s balmy climate was known as that: a balm. Rest and relaxation. Then, as now, Barbados is a fine place for R&R. It’s also become a great place for golf.

Golf.title: Is the bump-and-run *really* more reliable than a chip shot?
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Doug Spencer ran an experiment to find out if a bump-and-run is really more reliable than a chip shot. The post Is the bump-and-run *really* more reliable than a chip shot? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ditching high-loft wedges around the green in favor of a hybrid bump-and-run is one of golf’s classic pieces of advice, but do the numbers actually back it up? That was something I wondered recently, so I decided to conduct a small experiment.

We put three amateur players through a 30-shot test to see if putting with a hybrid produces better proximity and consistency than traditional wedge options. And not only did they test their mettle on both types of shots, when it came to the hybrid bump-and-run, this was their first time ever trying the shot.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia seeks exit from LIV Golf contract, while LIV Golf Australia venue says it hasn't been paid in court filings
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia seeks exit from LIV Golf contract, while LIV Golf Australia venue says it hasn't been paid in court filings Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Sergio Garcia is seeking official termination of his LIV Golf contract, according to new court filings. Last month, LIV Golf’s bankruptcy plea included a restructuring that would likely release LIV players from their existing contracts, allowing them to pursue opportunities elsewhere. Late Wednesday, Garcia’s lawyers and his LLC (Even Par) asserted they do not oppose this motion but do want clarification, as Garcia’s representation requests the court honor the request to end the agreement or allow Garcia to end it. As currently constructed, Garcia argues, the deal is confusing.

“So long as the Agreement remains of record, tournament organizers, sponsors, and other counterparties may hesitate before dealing with Garcia, who may be unable to represent that they are free of competing contractual commitments,” Garcia’s lawyers argue. “That uncertainty is particularly acute for a professional athlete, whose tournament schedule, sponsorship arrangements, and participation in other events must be planned well in advance, and whose competitive career is necessarily finite.”

Golf.title: Caolan Rafferty is Ireland's grand slam winner you don't know
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy won the career Grand Slam at Augusta in 2025. Six months later, amateur Caolan Rafferty became Ireland's other slam winner. The post Caolan Rafferty is Ireland’s grand slam winner you don’t know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In April of last year, Rory McIlroy crumpled to the ground at Augusta National, having finally won the Masters to complete the career Grand Slam. Six months later, the Isle of Ireland got another slam winner — one who has no equal. While McIlroy, who is from Northern Ireland, was the sixth member to join professional golf’s most prestigious club, Caolan Rafferty — who is from Dundalk, Ireland — is the only amateur ever to complete the “Provincial Slam” by winning the North, South, East, and West of Ireland championships.

The list of legendary Irish amateurs is long. The names include McIlroy, Shane Lowry, Darren Clarke, Padraig Harrington, J.B. Carr, John Burke and Hugh Foley, among others. And yet many of the biggest names didn’t have the extended amateur run that Rafferty has had, as they eventually turned to professional golf. Clarke and Foley won three of the four legs of the Provincial before turning pro. Lowry won two.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy confirms Abu Dhabi Championship return as Aldar named title partner
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy confirms Abu Dhabi Championship return as Aldar named title partner Golf Digest Middle East
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy will play the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links from November 5 to 8, the DP World Tour has confirmed. The announcement came alongside news that Aldar, the Abu Dhabi real estate developer that owns the course, has become title partner of the first of the season’s two Play-Off events. The tournament will now be known as the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy arrives as six-time major champion, the reigning Masters champion and the defending Race to Dubai champion. He has never won in Abu Dhabi. “I’ve finished runner-up here four times, so I’d obviously love to go one better and finally win it,” he said. “I really enjoy finishing my season in the UAE, and hopefully I can have a strong week and put myself in a position to win another Race to Dubai title.”

Golf.body:
It was never about invitations to the fanciest clubs, the biggest sponsorships or the nicest cars. In fact, for a time it seemed he would be remembered most as a side-door entrant: someone who didn’t mind gritting his teeth and grinding out par against more talented players, despite a gap in raw ability that was evident even to him.

“In a nutshell… I have felt like I have done more with less than most,” John Peterson told GOLF.com Tuesday from his truck, en route to pick up supplies for his farm in Texas. “I think that’s probably what I’m most proud about when I look back on my golf career.”

Golf.title: This psychedelic golf retreat is a trip in more ways than one
Golf.summary: Guests stay five nights at a luxe seaside home in Los Cabos with an expert ayahuasca practitioner on site around the clock. The post This psychedelic golf retreat is a trip in more ways than one appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Golf courses are full of hazards, but the game itself isn’t dangerous. It’s not high-speed like auto racing or high-impact like the NFL. While you might tweak your back or jam a wrist, the risk of lasting harm is vanishingly low.

So why, when you play, are you so often afraid? Christopher Smith has long wrestled with the question. A GOLF Top 100 Teacher who has been an instructor for more than 35 years, Smith knows that sound mechanics can calm the heebie-jeebies (it’s not a bad idea to take a lesson!), and that mental strength can be a salve (nothing wrong with seeing a sports psychologist!). But he believes getting to the source of fear and discomfort sometimes requires going deeper.

Scotland's number one golfer, Robert MacIntyre, has called for Carnoustie and Muirfield to become regular venues again for the Open Championship. Carnoustie last hosted the tournament in 2018, when Italy's Francesco Molinari lifted the Claret Jug, while Muirfield's most recent staging was in 2013.

Next year's Open will be held at St Andrews and MacIntyre says more regular visits to Scotland would be a major boost for the game in the country. "That would be brilliant," he said. "I feel like there's not enough Open Championships in Scotland anymore.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's endless quest has him frustrated after 'pretty shocking' week in France
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland hoped he was close to finding his old self, but one illuminating quote in France shows his endless quest continues to drag on. The post Viktor Hovland’s endless quest has him frustrated after ‘pretty shocking’ week in France appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Last month, Viktor Hovland’s PGA Tour season ended with a near-miss at the Tour Championship. It was a week that started with Hovland finding “something’ that allowed him to “hit the ball straight” to vault into contention at East Lake. Hovland was in position to win entering the final round but stalled, shooting 2-over as Scottie Scheffler caught and passed him to take the title.

Hovland has been in search mode for a while. He has won each of the past two seasons with the combination of a hot putter and a knack for competition, but that’s not what he’s looking for. He’s looking for something that is both familiar and foreign: who he used to be.

Golf.body:
For the average recreational golfer, the commonly cited odds of making a hole-in-one are approximately 12,500 to 1. For an albatross, or double eagle — a 2 on a par 5 — it’s approximately 6 million to 1.

Those odds are 1 in 14.5 quadrillion, according to one computation, which we’ll explain in a moment. In other words, virtually impossible. And yet — you guessed it — it happened.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: What's the maximum number of penalty strokes you can accrue on 1 shot?
Golf.summary: Is there a limit to the number of penalty strokes you can accrue by hitting a single tee shot? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: What’s the maximum number of penalty strokes you can accrue on 1 shot? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Hypothetical question: How many penalty strokes could a player get from hitting one tee shot? My thought: He’s late for his tee time, asks his opponent what club he used, tees it up in front of the marker, has too many clubs in his bag, uses an illegal club or ball, and then hits it out of bounds. Your thoughts? —Todd Sherstad, via email

First thought: Rules Guy needs more coffee to tackle this convoluted theoretical, but then sufficient caffeine kicked in. In 2023, Rule 1.3c(4) was designed to help limit the number of penalty strokes players could accumulate between strokes, so long as they were unaware of the breaches at the time. Thus, theoretically, absent that awareness, a player should only be able to rack up three penalty strokes in one shot — two for a breach and one for stroke and distance after hitting it out of bounds.

Golf.body:
Wherever there’s a lighthouse, it’s common to find a links nearby. No wonder, really. The same rugged shores that pose a risk to ships are often ideal grounds for golf. Take the South Ayrshire coast of Scotland, home to a fabled championship layout and one of the best-known beacons in the game.

A postcard staple for generations, and now a star of countless Instagram feeds, the Turnberry Lighthouse cuts a striking profile beside the 9th hole of Trump Turnberry, overlooking the Ailsa Course and the Firth of Clyde, with humpbacked Ailsa Craig rising like a half-moon on the horizon.

Usually, LIV players can be identified via their team's apparel, with individuals contractually obliged to wear their side's clothing, even in non-LIV events. This week, over 20 golfers from the circuit are playing in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship and, during a practice round on Tuesday, one of those was seen without LIV branding.

Badminton.title: Debutants Cyprus Relish Opening Experience
Badminton.summary: Debutants Cyprus Relish Opening Experience BWF
Badminton.body:
It wasn’t a bad debut for Cyprus at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026. Three-time champions Korea did beat them comfortably but the first-timers registered their presence as the 22nd edition of the Suhandinata Cup got underway at the Cairo International Stadium.

Coach Shai Geffen was pleased with his team’s performance against the Asian powerhouse. “This is a big opportunity,” said Geffen. “It’s a first time for us participating in any World Championships as a team. So this is a good opportunity for the players to understand the culture of badminton – not just in Europe. We could play Korea, a powerhouse of Asia, and we’ll play Denmark, one of the best teams in the world. So this is a big challenge. But to see where we are and how we can improve.

Badminton.title: Indonesia opens Suhadinata Cup campaign with 2-0 win over Azerbaijan
Badminton.summary: Indonesia opens Suhadinata Cup campaign with 2-0 win over Azerbaijan ANTARA News
Badminton.body:
Indonesia secured both 55-point relay games with scores of 55-25 and 55-11, recording its first victory in the contest for the Suhandinata Cup. "The first match is never easy," Indonesian team manager Eskar Denatara said in a statement released by the Indonesian Badminton Association (PBSI) on Monday.

He noted that several players were still adapting to conditions at Cairo International Stadium during the first game, particularly regarding draft and lighting. In the first game, Indonesia took the lead through mixed doubles pair Moses Andar Simanjuntak and Reya Azzahra Yulianti, who put the Red and White team ahead 11-5 over Ulvi Huseynov and Leyla Jamalzade.

Badminton.title: A Father’s Death, and a Team That Became Family
Badminton.summary: A Father’s Death, and a Team That Became Family BWF
Badminton.body:
Exactly a year ago, Azerbaijan’s Ulvi Huseynov was going on court for his men’s singles final at a regional championships when he felt an inexplicable heaviness in his right shoulder while picking up his racket bag.

He did lose that match, and he remembers how quiet the team bus was on their way back to the hotel. He was asked to leave for home immediately, and only on getting there did he realise why the management had insisted he skip the prize ceremony later that day – his father had passed away.

Badminton.title: ‘It’s a Dream Coming True’
Badminton.summary: ‘It’s a Dream Coming True’ BWF
Badminton.body:
Egypt is on the cusp of making history, and Hadia Hosny couldn’t be happier. Cairo plays host to the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 – the biggest tournament ever held in the country. The three-time Olympian, former Member of the Egyptian Parliament, and now the President of the Egyptian Badminton Federation, talks of the significance of hosting the tournament:

What does it mean for you to have a tournament of this scale in Egypt? This is the first time ever we’re having a very big tournament like this. It means a lot. I was wishing this since I was an athlete and I feel like I’m the one on court right now (laughs).

Badminton.title: Suhandinata Cup Redraw: Korea Grouped With Denmark
Badminton.summary: Suhandinata Cup Redraw: Korea Grouped With Denmark BWF
Badminton.body:
Three-time champions Korea are grouped with European power Denmark at the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships 2026 that will start in Cairo on Monday 5 October. The redraw for the World Junior Championships, necessitated by the withdrawals of Nigeria and Macau China after the original draw in August, was held today.

Korea, Denmark and debutants Cyprus are in Group H2, while Group H1 has second seeds Thailand, debutants Senegal, and Brazil. Defending champions China, the 5/8 seeds, are in Group E1 with South Africa and Zambia; Group E2 consists of Turkiye, Mauritius and Zimbabwe.

Badminton.title: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joshua Muguluma Richard
Badminton.summary: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joshua Muguluma Richard BWF
Badminton.body:
This is the 75th story in our Humans of Shuttle Time series, in which we present the perspectives of those who are involved with badminton at the grassroots level. Joshua Muguluma Richard, Shuttle Time Tutor with Uganda Badminton Association, talks of his journey in badminton.

I was born in Uganda, Kampala as the second of three boys. My childhood was shaped by simple living with strong family values and support from my parents. Growing up, I learned the importance of respect, hard work, and kindness from people around me. My social background was influenced a lot by the community I lived in, especially my neighbours who knew each other well and often helped one another during difficult times.

Badminton.title: World Juniors: Africa Beckons
Badminton.summary: World Juniors: Africa Beckons BWF
Badminton.body:
When the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships begin in Egypt on Monday 5 October, it will mark only the second time ever that the tournament has visited Africa. It has been 24 years since Pretoria in South Africa hosted the world’s premier junior tournament. With the 26th edition of the World Juniors, badminton in Africa is poised to make a big leap, entering new territory as it were. Participation from the continent is at a high – nine countries have entered.

Of the 47 teams competing at the BWF World Junior Team Championships for the Suhandinata Cup, 19 from Europe, 13 from Asia, four from Pan Am, and two from Oceania, besides nine from Africa.

Badminton.body:
Kunlavut Vitidsarn celebrated his return to the top of the world rankings by defeating Loh Kean Yew 21-12 21-16 for the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games gold medal on Tuesday. Both players had already made history by becoming their countries’ first men’s singles finalists. But Vitidsarn went one step further, denying Loh the rare feat of defeating two top-ranked players after the Singaporean had beaten Jonatan Christie in the quarterfinals.

“Really happy because I didn’t come here thinking about a medal. My (recent) performances haven’t been good enough,” admitted Vitidsarn. “Being world No.1 brings a lot of pressure because everyone thinks, ‘You are No. 1, how could you lose like this?’ It’s very difficult.”

Competitor News.title: Standard Chartered turns F1 strategy into a brand story
Competitor News.summary: Standard Chartered turns F1 strategy into a brand story ContentGrip
Competitor News.body:
Standard Chartered has moved its Formula 1 partnership from sponsorship asset to brand story. Its new global campaign, "Move Ahead", does not focus only on speed, cars or race-day spectacle. Instead, the bank uses the preparation behind Formula 1 as a metaphor for how clients make decisions, manage risk and move across markets.

That distinction matters for marketers. Sports sponsorships often stop at access, logos and hospitality. Standard Chartered is trying to turn the behavior of the sport itself into a way to explain what the brand does.
